text_translated_detailed: The arrival of Constantijn Sebens, who was appointed First Administrator by the departing merchant and First Administrator of the Islands, has brought about the proper transfer of the warehouses and the Company's effects contained therein. He has taken his seat in our political and judicial council and is prepared to proceed with the aforementioned vessel with a cargo of the ship De Lis, which was sent to Rembang on the east coast of Java on the 27th of March 1745. The merchant Loten is proceeding to Batavia with the ship Dorgwyk, which lies in cargo, and has properly delivered here such cash, beverages, and goods as are mentioned in the received bill of lading and invoice. For the sending of these we express our humble thanks, and we have provided the Surabaya office with its portion. Meanwhile, the bearer of this has received his cargo consisting of 280 loads of rice, 29 bales of cotton yarn, 2000 pieces of legger duijgen [uncertain: type of cloth or material], yielding ƒ19,547:16:8. As evidenced by the attached bills of lading, vessel and pearl invoice paired with two cost calculations and extracts from our aforementioned council decisions dated the 10th and 16th of this month, it appears that the ship De Lis received provisioning, arrack, and further refreshment for its sick crew members, just as the ship De Peer received the same. The two last-mentioned vessels, being the aforementioned vessel which was sent to Rembang to receive its cargo, amounting to the sums of ƒ400:9:8 and ƒ230:5, which amounts we humbly renew the request made by the resident for spikes and bar iron on the east coast of Java on the 27th of March 1741. And the Shed of the seafarers and craftsmen, made of wooden posts and bamboo and covered with atap, since the aforementioned Line has fallen in for a great part, and all the rest so by the white ants consumed and by Age worm-eaten and decayed, that a total collapse threatens, just as also the Company's hospital, whereby the same requires a notable repair, since its foundations and all the walls have separated from one another through the sinking and cracking of the ground, and the surrounding walls have already fallen away in part. The one and the other would, according to Exact calculation, come to cost ƒ 39,862:15— [modern equivalent: Dutch guilders], under which reckoned that which now, as aforesaid, is merely of bamboo, must also be made strong of stone and covered with tiles, so that the Company might enjoy the required service from it for a long time. Meanwhile, it is further humbly requested of Your Honored and Esteemed that in place of the palisading laid down here a year ago, the Hope [uncertain: possibly a ship name or facility name] this Office may be provided with another and two more such small vessels, so that upon occurring occasions they may be employed. From Java's East Coast under date 27 March 1741. Finally, it serves to notify Your Honored and Esteemed that the guardians of the Sumanap's chief Regent Radeen Tommongong T. Sacranagara, Radeen Ajoe Soeradinin-grat, and her husband Radeen Aria Soera Dieningrat, with their retinue, on the 30th of the aforementioned month of January, arrived here from Semarang, and on the 4th of the current [month] undertook the journey again to Sumanap, whereby we remain with much respect. Undersigned. Title. Lower. Your Honored and Esteemed

text_translated_detailed: Of Java's east coast, dated 27 March 1741— Copy Samarang [Semarang:] To the Honored and Esteemed Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, Chief Merchant and Governor over Java's northeast coast, together with the council there. — Your Honored Self's missives dated 25 February last and 8 current have been received by me. The first on the 2nd of this month by the Assistant Elizes Cholle and Sergeant Jan Huijser, as replacements for the aforementioned Assistant Agidius van Braam and Sergeant Pieter van Hekelen, who departed on the 3rd thereof with Your Honored Self's missive to Surabaya. The last mentioned on the 10th thereof by the Constable's Mate Anthonij Hulser and the soldier Johanne Blank, with the Constable Arij Eijsbrands, according to earlier orders, locked in the stocks, under the supervision of Corporal Thomas Scholsteijn and two other military men to Your Honored Self's [authority]. I have also immediately had the received name roll of the Chinese Rebels delivered to the Javanese regents and shall conduct myself in all respect according to the further received papers. The 4 Pantjallangs are at Your Honored Self's disposition of Java's east coast, dated 27 March 1741, ready, as I hope, also of the 6 Chialouppen [uncertain: possibly a type of vessel or military unit] towards the end of May or the 15th of June, if the iron and nails are obtained in this month, and two ordered schooners for Japara are also begun, at 9 [uncertain: possibly a measurement or cost]. I have warned the Chinese Koe Sonko that he must betake himself there, with which this brief [letter] concludes, and I remain with respect [undersigned] Title [lower] Your Honored Self's obedient and obedient servant [was signed] P„r de benzin [in margin] Rembang, the 12th March, Year 1741: P.S. I request most humbly to know what cost allowance the Constable's Mate Anthonij Hulscher shall receive [undersigned] Agreed L Barenclouw [was signed] Secretary. — Register of the

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast, the 27th of March 1741. Circular Letter to the Offices at Kartasura [Cartasoera], Surabaya [Sourabaija], Pasuruan [Passourouang], Rembang, Jepara [Japara], Demak [Damak], Joana, and Tagal. Title. Your Excellency: Being aware that a conspiracy of discontented Chinese here on Java has rebelled against the Company and has not refrained from using hostilities, for the destruction of which the Susuhunan has given the necessary orders to his Regents, and through whose vigilance 4 heads and two persons of that murderous conspiracy have already been brought in and the latter have also been executed here, of which one delinquent, Nio Tietko, under confession given, has revealed the names of the "cast-off head and lesser ones" of this abominable conspiracy, named on the annexed name roll, thus it is hereby ordered to Your Excellency that the native Regents under Your Excellency's district shall immediately provide proper notice and communicate the aforementioned name list, so that those villains may also be apprehended and brought into the hands of Justice, which will be very easy, since they are known by their hair and clothing sufficiently, with which we remain under friendly greetings [underlined] Your Excellency's good friends [signed] R. C. von Glan, Joan Gidean Loten, G. H. Alexhelt, I. M. v. d. Heyden, P. Devos, and J. Tonneman, Junior [in margin] Semarang, the 8th of March 1741. [underlined] Agrees P. L. Barenclouw [signed] Notary, — Semarang, To the Esteemed and Honored Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, chief merchant and governor, on and along Java's north-east coast.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast on the 3rd of April 1741. At Samarang. To the Esteemed and Respected Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, chief merchant and commander on and along Java's North and East Coast, together with the Council. Sir, your esteemed letters of the 8th and 14th of this month have been duly received by me, and according to your esteemed order I have given the Javanese Regents proper notice of the Susuhunan's [modern equivalent: the Sunan of Surakarta], and your esteemed order regarding the rebellious Chinese, as I have also distributed the good months to the postholders here stationed according to the enclosed receipt roll. I have also had the honor to declare my obligation for the orders shared by their Most Noble Lordships, according to which I shall conduct myself dutifully. From Java's East Coast on the 3rd of April 1741. By the ship Enkhuijsen, here brought 20,000 Rixdollars [modern equivalent: Rixdollars], according to the accompanying invoice, has also taken from here 416 loads of rice and 8,000 pounds of tail pepper, amounting according to the enclosed invoice to ƒ 29,903:1:—, with which that vessel returned from here on the 20th, and during the time of lying at anchor on the same there died and here was buried the third mate Jasper Jansen Smit of Christiania and the high boatswain Michael Radewant of Anklam, the first having made his will here before his death, whose disposition in copy is attached herewith, whereby I wish, as God's dear rod shall wish, as I have had the honor with many conclusions to be [undersigned] Sir, [lower] respectfully your esteemed obedient and obedient Servant [signed] L. Grothe, [in margin] Tagal, the 25th of March 1741. [undersigned] Agrees. By L. Baeren Clouw, secretary.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast, the 30th of April 1741. [Undersigned:] Agrees [was signed:] P.r L: BaerenClouw, secretary. To the Adipatti Thitlaasoema, eastern strand governor at Japara [Jepara:]. After customary preliminaries, whereas a conspiracy of ill-intentioned Chinese under a new leader by the name of Ian Siko, without and with shaved heads, yet with customary weapons, have committed hostilities at Tanjong anew and continue to hold themselves there, and I have therefore issued the necessary orders to Adipatti Astrawidjaja, chief remitter, and the here present regents: Adipatti djasijnde strand jadiningaat, Radeen Soeralaija, Radeen Soerenggrana, the tommangongs Tsjaccra, djaja, wiera sestra and rastanagara, and Radeen Kiaij Rongo of Caliewoengoe, who together this evening are sending out a command of 540 armed Javanese of their subordinates in order to capture or destroy the aforementioned vagabonds at once, and to make this effect all the better, I have also arranged the required [gesz: uncertain] to the regents of Coedoes, Pattijen Tjankalsewoe, of which one and the other I hereby give Your Excellency notice, not doubting your and Your Excellency's vigilance, the more so since it is strengthened by the prince's order. — All that I have to say on this occasion is contained in this letter, which is signed at the head office Samarang on the 29th of April in the year 1741. [Undersigned:] Agrees [was signed:] r P: Z: Baeren Clouw: secretary. To the Demang of Tanjong.

Besides this, we have understood the further contents; but what troubles our heart is that Your Honored, together with Djajaningrat and his confederates from the coastal regents, who are all at Semarang, have decided to send 540 armed carriers to Tanjong, and as their commander is Perangbaija from Paccalongan [Pekalongan: coastal town]. That which most moves us and makes our heart uneasy is not that we are unwilling to help the Company in its difficulties, but because the coastal regents have sent their people to Tanjong contrary to custom and contrary to our orders—that is, Brother, what makes our heart uneasy. And because thereafter many Javanese would be emboldened to go against the orders of the prince without our authority, and thereby lose their power, therefore, Brother, we now request that such a thing may not happen again in the future, and that of all that which the Honored Company requests, without fail our knowledge be given first, for Java stands under our obedience.

Chinese planks and for transport thither of bar iron and nails destined for the Evengemelt [uncertain: possibly a place name or administrative term] comptoir. In the meantime, we have taken into consideration that these Surabaya recently delivered 300 coijangs [uncertain: unit of measurement] and remnants of rice in Chinese houses at the expense of the Honored Company are stored and through the length of time would become spoiled, and having taken into account that this grain is presently required at the Indian chief place, just as it is to be presumed that few ships will appear here on Java in this year for the collection of the remaining products, we have deemed it good, under favorable consideration, to order the Surabaya servants to send the aforementioned grain by inland vessels to Batavia, provided that the freight is negotiated to the advantage of the Company. Den onderkoopman g zoldij boekhouder Pieter De Vos; Den onderkoopman en fiscaal — Jeronimus Sonnemands Junior Aangesien de sourabaijse bediendens bij schrijven van den 18: 8ber: a:o pass:o versogt hebben, dat de aldaar Jongst geleverde 300: coijangs en restanten van rijst in Chineese huijsen ten lasten van d' EComp: op geschuurt per jnlandse vaartuijgen na Batavia mogte overgesonden, mitsgaders in aanmerkinge dient genoomen te werden dat dien graan tegens tegenwoor dig ter voors hooftplaatse necessaire werd gerequireerde en daar het lang leggen bedorven zoude geraaken, soo mede om d' EComp: te bevrijden van Een swaare huurloon temeer te persumeeren is dat weijnig scheepen hier op Java in dit Jaar sullen verscheijnen ter afhaal der resteerende producten Van Iavas oostcust den 6:' Maij 1741 zoo is na voorgaande deliberatie, over de voorsz: omstandigheeden goedgevonden de sourabaijse bediendens bij Een brief te gelasten het voorenstaande prompt te Effectueeren, mits dat den vragt ten voordeele van d' Ecomp:e werd bedongen en dat hier van Eerbiedig kenniss sal gegeeven werden aan hoog moeten gemelte haar Edelheedens /onderstond:/ smarang Jn Rade dato voorsz: /:was getek:d D„k Visscher, R: C: von Glan, Const„n Rus Sibens, G:t Alephelb: C: M: V: d: Heijden, J: d: Vos, en Jeronimus Tonneman Jutior; /:onderstond:/ Accordeert, J„n L: Haeren Clouw /
text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast on the 6th of May 1741: B[artholomeus] Visscher, R[udolph] C[arel] Von Glan, [and:] Const[antijn] Sibens, G[errit] Alephelt[: S[teven] M[arcus] v[an] d[er] Heijden, P[ieter] Vos, and J[eronimus] Tonnemans Junior, Samarang on the 6th of May [in margin:] A[nno] 1791. Wednesday the 5th of April 1741, in the morning at nine o'clock. Present: The chief merchant and governor of this Coast Bartholomeus Visscher, The Captain Rudolph Carel von Glan, The merchant and first administrator Constantijn Siebens, The lieutenant Gerrit Hendrik Alephelt, The under-merchant and second administrator Steven Marcus van der Heijden, From Java's East Coast on the 6th of May 1741. The under-merchant and salary bookkeeper Pieter De Vos; The under-merchant and fiscal officer Jeronimus Sonnemands Junior. Whereas the Surabaya servants have requested by letter of the 18th of August in the year past that the recently delivered 300 coijangs and remnants of rice in Chinese houses at the expense of the Honored Company stored there might be sent by inland vessels to Batavia, and likewise it should be taken into consideration that this grain is presently required at the aforementioned chief place and that it would become spoiled through long storage, and also to relieve the Honored Company of a heavy rental fee, all the more so since it is to be presumed that few ships will appear here on Java in this year for the collection of the remaining products. From Java's East Coast on the 6th of May 1741, after the aforementioned deliberation regarding the aforementioned circumstances, it has been deemed good to order the Surabaya servants by a letter to promptly execute the aforementioned matter, provided that the freight is negotiated to the advantage of the Honored Company and that respectful notice of this shall be given to the aforementioned High Esteemed Gentlemen [understood:] Samarang. text_translated_detailed: A small boat from Shoream [uncertain: possibly a place name], mounted with 8 small iron cannon pieces and manned with eleven men of his nation to fetch pepper, in such manner with a cargo of white pepper, by estimation five last [modern equivalent: approximately 10,000 pounds] of the house or from there undertaking a journey, was hindered by heavy weather and contrary winds from Java's east coast on the 6th of May 1741. It came to be stranded, reaching as far as the south side of this island and further after much struggling through the Bali Strait on the 21st of last week came to be beached, through Grisee [Gresik], with great leakage and lack of provisions, for which he was provided with cash payment, and furthermore the aforementioned small vessel, which they have until now kept afloat through constant pumping, was hauled onto the shore there in order to caulk it somewhat if possible and make it tight, but this was found not to be feasible, because while one leak was being stopped, another new one would open up. Captain Hughes testifies that the small boat is 23 years old, and for that reason the costs would not be worth what would be required to bring it back into serviceable condition, besides which the aforementioned sailors, who are now mostly sick, would not dare to venture back to sea from Java's east coast on the 6th of May 1741, and he would not be able to justify such a renewal to his lords and masters, and because that small vessel, which is mostly worm-eaten and decayed, eaten through by the worm, he has entirely rejected, presenting the aforementioned pepper for good payment to the Company, in order that from the proceeds thereof he might here purchase another vessel to be able to undertake his detained journey to Bencoolen [Bengkulu] again, for which one and another respectfully requests the approval of your honors, also permission from your honors that the aforementioned Hughes may sell his present condemned small boat here to the highest bidder.

text_translated_detailed: On the 10th of May 1741. From four heads 4000 rixdollars [modern equivalent: silver currency] and on the dead heads 2000 rixdollars, His Majesty has in a letter in response expressed himself very graciously and courteously and has approved in all respects my proposed plan, and for the destruction of the aforementioned rabble, has sent hither four strand regents [regional rulers], namely those of Suban, Caliwoengoe, Candal, and Grobogan, strengthened with their armed retainers, which according to a separate letter from the commandant at Cartasoera to me, dated the 4th of this month, are estimated at 6000 heads, of which the copy together with one from the 2nd before is enclosed herewith, containing principally the disposition concerning the aforementioned "nangs" expedition, and that His Majesty has declared himself very gladly and cheerfully to be fully assured and satisfied with the contents of my letters, which is further evident from the enclosed original missive and its Dutch translation, continuing further that His Highness has seen fit that his strand regents appeared at the stipulated time, requesting meanwhile that I should communicate to your High Excellency without delay that His Majesty's Javanese are now being sent to strike the hostile Chinese at Tanjong, so that on this occasion the Javanese subjects who perform this service for the Company might be remembered, in respect to when something is requested of the Company, in accordance with what is reasonable, since it has never happened that the Javanese have performed such service for the Company, with no further circumstances extended in the aforementioned letter. From Java's East Coast, the 10th of May 1741. This being so, and from consideration of the reasons cited in my previous separate writing, I request by this very humbly your High Excellency's permission, most esteemed and honored, to be able to publish an act of amnesty, in order to be able to preserve the good Chinese.

text_translated_detailed: the stipulated time have arrived. Moreover, brother, the same letter mentions that Your Esteemed [person] requested our help to send people from Java's East Coast, the 10th of May 1741, to strike the evil-doing Chinese who have assembled themselves at Tanjong. And by the second letter Your Esteemed [person] requests our help with the greatest speed, because Your Esteemed [person] is not at ease of heart, for the rumors go that the evil Chinese at Tanjong grow more and more numerous, and that the sent-out Javanese have attacked them, but one does not know who has won or lost the battle. Brother, be not doubtful, for we shall certainly, insofar as it lies in our power, help the Esteemed Company, since we are a true friend and ally of the Esteemed Company, and this is also concluded in the contracts which we have entered into with the Esteemed Company. Moreover, the Javanese realm and the Esteemed Company are one body. Over this, we shall send to strike the Chinese at Tanjong from our beach regents, namely Ranga from Java's East Coast, the 10th of May 1741, Dimangala of Caliewoengoe, the Ingabij Awang of Candal, the Tommongong Sucradiningrat of Toeban, and the Ingabij Martadipoera of Grobogan, whom we have all ordered to take the route over Samarang to meet Your Esteemed [person]. Furthermore, brother, Your Esteemed [person] has been pleased to ask us for our concept and consent regarding that Your Esteemed [person] was inclined to let a placard go out, because half of that nation are forced by four heads named Ian Sinko, Que Peko, Lim Toko, and Ijo-Sienko. On the aforementioned heads, a premium of 4000 rixdollars [modern equivalent: guilders] is to be placed for the one who brings them all four alive into hand, and dead 2000 rixdollars, and that Your Esteemed [person] excludes no nation therein, but whoever it is who brings the aforementioned heads will certainly receive the premium.

text_translated_detailed: there was an edict issued because half of that nation was forced by four leaders named Ian sinko, que peko, Lim Toko, and ijo-Sienko to place a premium of 4000 rixdollars [modern equivalent: Dutch colonial currency] on the aforementioned leaders for whoever brings all four of them alive into our hands, and 2000 rixdollars for dead ones, and that no nation whatsoever is excepted from this, but whoever brings the aforementioned leaders will certainly receive the premium according to the content of the edict, so that a speedy end comes to it. From Java's east coast on the 10th of May 1741. Your Excellency has agreed to this rightly, and we concur completely with Your Excellency. Meanwhile, brother, we request that Your Excellency be pleased to communicate without fail to the great father the Governor-General and the assembled Noble Lords of the Council of India that we are now sending Javanese to strike the Chinese at Tanjong, so that from today or tomorrow onwards our Javanese subjects who perform service for the Company may be remembered, that we make this request, brother, is because we have understood that in the time of our deceased great father and father it never happened that the Javanese performed service for the Company as they do now, and since we perceive that Javanese in many places perform service for the Company, and therefore perhaps tomorrow or the day after they may well request something in the reasonableness of the Company, that we make this known, brother, from Java's east coast on the 10th of May 1741. / because we are a sincere friend and ally of the Company. Wednesday the 3rd of May, Anno 1741, in the forenoon at 9 o'clock. Present: the head merchant and governor of this coast Bartholomeus Visscher, the Captain Rudolph Carel van Glan, the merchant and first administrator Constantijn Sibens, the lieutenant Gerrit Hendrik Alphelt, the under-merchant and second administrator Steven Markus van der Heyden, and the under-merchant and soldier account-keeper Pieter de Vos, and the under-merchant and fiscal Jeronimus Tonneman Junior. The lieutenant of the Chinese, Que Jonko, was arrested and brought into the lodge. When questioned regarding his flight from Java's east coast on the 10th of May 1741, he could give no reason except that he had been, as it were, struck in the head yesterday afternoon and had gone alone to Patterongan, where he sat under a tree the entire night until early morning, when he returned to his house and found that his wife and children, slaves and slave women, had already escaped. And since one still has no reason to declare him innocent, but the flight does make him suspect, it has been unanimously decided to place him in the lodge under civil arrest. text_translated_detailed: [signed:] I. L. BaerenClouw, secretary. Tuesday the 2nd of May 1741, in the afternoon at half past three o'clock. From Java's east coast, the 10th of May 1741. Present: the head merchant and governor of this coast Bartholomeus Visscher, the Captain Rudolph Carel von Glan, the Captain and first administrator Constantijn Sibens, the lieutenant Gerrit Hendrik Alphelt, the under-merchant and second administrator Steven Marcus van der Heyden, the under-merchant and soldier account-keeper Pieter de Vos, and the under-merchant and fiscal Jeronimus Tonneman Junior. The meeting being prevented, the governor gave notice that the lieutenant of the Chinese, Que Jonko, had at 12 o'clock secretly absconded with his household, principal goods, slaves, pikes, and muskets without anyone knowing where he had taken his course. Of which the Captain Anko first gave notice at half past three o'clock from Java's east coast on the 10th of March 1741. And since this case appears very strange, especially as he had made the most solemn protestations that he would never be disloyal to his Captain and would remain loyal to the Company until the last drop of blood, even though the rebellious members of his nation rage, consideration has been given to what should be done in such cases, especially since one cannot know from what intention the lieutenant has taken flight, or whether there is not a snake hidden beneath it, and also from Damak unfavorable news has come that the enemy troops are approaching and intend to strike their camp at Goemalak. And after careful deliberation it has been decided that the house of the lieutenant shall be searched and the goods found there shall be brought into the lodge. Furthermore, the fiscal, as chief officer, shall remain outside to have direction over the natives and burgers taken into service and their patrol, strengthened with an ensign, two sergeants, two corporals, and a piper from Java's east coast on the 10th of March 1741 at three o'clock, notice

Your Honour's esteemed [person], please be so kind as to order, and furthermore, if Your Honour's esteemed [person] should judge that the force was too small, the realm's administrator should then send more troops. Meanwhile, yesterday morning the aforementioned Ajoe Gilang, wife of the aforementioned Pangerang Ingabeij, was delivered of a son in childbed, and I hereby testify with deep respectful regard to be [subordinate]. Title [lower]. Your Honour's esteemed [person], most obedient and humble servant, [was signed] J.s van Velse. [In margin] Samarang, 16th May, Year 1742, in the evening at seven o'clock. P.S. From Java's East Coast, 20th May 1741, whereby the accompanying letter to this message was lost, as Your Honour's esteemed [person] will be pleased to hear from the aforementioned Javanese. Java's East Coast, 20th May 1741. After the customary preliminaries, furthermore brother, I bring to Your Honour's knowledge that I have been ordered to have the prince's revenues from the toll stations collected, particularly those of the captain of the Chinese of Samarang, and if it can be done and if the same can be done with a peaceful mind, so I request that he proceed to Cartasoera, as well as the other Chinese who, besides the captain, have leased [revenues] from His Majesty. And brother, if Your Honour does not wish to allow this with a peaceful heart, then I request that the captain or other Chinese who have anything from the prince's lease send their envoys to pay the lease monies. Furthermore brother, regarding satisfying the Chinese at Tanjong or elsewhere on Java who trouble Your Honour's heart, from Java's East Coast, 20th May 1741, I have had no troubled mind about this for weeks, for His Majesty has sent his subjects to Your Honour's aid. Finally, brother, I have received orders from the prince regarding that His Majesty has an inclination toward a Chinese daughter who is beautiful and well-formed. Brother, such a matter is beyond my power to seek out. Therefore I request Your Honour's aid, whether there might be a daughter of the wicked Chinese who is worthy to be offered to the prince.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast, 20th May 1741. After the customary preliminaries, Your Honour, my brothers, very dear and obliging letter, I have received in due time, from which I have seen with satisfaction that through Your Honour's vigilance, both for the service of the Susuhunang as well as that of his Ally, everything had been brought into readiness for the destruction of the ill-disposed Chinese, to the mutual peace. Now to communicate that the necessary strand regents, the tommonmaij:ts gongs of Caliwongoe, Kandal, Toeban, and the Ingabeij of Grobogan have arrived here, having also orders according to their own account to destroy the enemy Chinese from the roads or similar places. After their troops were not yet complete, to gather which would still require about 4 days. From Java's East Coast, 20th May 1741. Meanwhile, they sent their mantries five days ago to reconnoiter regarding the strength, actions, and intentions of the aforementioned rebels, but have not yet returned. Of which another [matter] the Susuhunang maintains, the expedition of those sent shall [proceed], when the standing regents have been effectuated, so that to avoid much writing, [His Majesty's] complete answer can be [given]. His Majesty's youngest [son] here received with all honour the latest missive.

text_translated_detailed: Rosback received in the evening a separate letter from Their High Excellencies dated the 7th of this month, whereby it is ordered that from this garrison of Java's east coast, the 2nd of May 1741, under the command of Ensign Meijerhof, to detach to Tanjong a number of at least 50 European soldiers, reinforced with 100 Balians, Macassarese, and Buginese under a capable and good officer, to the end that, should such be deemed at all possible from there, to establish themselves, pursue, and root out the rebellious Chinese gathered there, to prevent the damage which from a continued stay and increasing strength of those ruffians will flow forth for the Company. Furthermore, that 50 Europeans are to come from Batavia at the first opportunity, likewise that the Samarang garrison shall be strengthened at a later opportunity with 200 Balians and Buginese, and furthermore furnished with cash and the requested 6,000 pounds [modern equivalent: approximately 2,700 kg] of gunpowder. Which from Java's east coast, the 20th of May 1741, aforementioned matter was taken into careful deliberation, and since the European garrison consists solely of 90 common healthy soldiers, and thus by sending 50 men, the remainder would not be the Company's lodging capable of being able to defend in case of unforeseen events, much less when 100 natives were also detached to Tanjong, and thereby the number of 150 men is much too weak to root out that rabble, especially since one cannot know the true strength of the enemy Chinese, but well that they are conjoined according to various reports with a party of Javanese, to which is added that the four sent Susuhunang's regents named Ranga Padimangala of Caliwoengoe, Ingabij Wongo of Candal, Radeen Tommongong Soeradering of Toeban, and Ingabeij Marta Poura of Grobogan, from Java's east coast, the 20th of May 1741, to the end as aforesaid, have declared that their people are far from being brought to completeness, and thus possibly still 6 or more days shall be delayed.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast, the 20th of May 1741. / Copy. To the Susuhunan Pakubuwono [Pakubuwono II], maintaining his court at Kartasura [Kartasura]. After customary preliminaries. Your Majesty's very kind letter I have received, and from it I understood that the regents of Caliwoengoe [Cirebon], Joeban [Juana], Kandal, and Grobogan had received orders from your Highness to strike the hostile Chinese at Tanjong [Tanjung]. For this courtesy I express my due obligation, and have immediately given notice thereof to their High Excellencies, as well as of the further contents of the aforementioned missive concerning your Majesty's subjects who render service for the Company, so that they might be remembered when they come to make a reasonable request of the Esteemed Company. In the meantime, I have the honor to communicate to your Majesty from Java's East Coast, the 20th of May 1741, that the aforementioned regents are still here, and declare that their peoples, consisting according to their own statement of 850 armed men, will be able to become fully ready within 6 or more days to carry out that Expedition. Furthermore, the aforementioned High Excellencies have ordered me to send a party of Europeans and native soldiers to Tanjong for the aforementioned purpose, which shall proceed when the peoples of your Majesty's Regents shall have been brought into readiness together. All that I have to say for this time is contained in this letter, which is signed at the main office Semarang [Semarang] on the 20th of May in the year 1741. / was signed / B. B[aron] Visscher. / undersigned / Agrees / was signed / S. L. Barenclouw, secretary.

Whereupon the deponents jointly decided, as it being impossible to offer resistance to such a mighty number, to travel down the river with 5 vessels and to seek a good refuge for the preservation of their lives, so that the said Chinese, perceiving the flight of the deponents, upon their gunfire, which was answered by them through the sergeant Robert Cammel, the corporals Gerrit van Leusden and Christoffel Rinsen, the soldiers David Lemke, Jurgen Harbril, Michiel Engelsz, Mensz, Martijn Geneke, Arnoud van Outuaven, and Pieter Soer with their muskets, until the deponents came outside the mouth of the river and the said rebels went out of sight. From Java's East Coast, the 2nd of June, 1741, the deponents remained there until evening to see whether the aforementioned sergeant Cammel and the last-mentioned men from whose vessels the Javanese had already jumped into the river might come forth, but perceiving nothing whatsoever of them, they set their course towards the residence of Rembang, which they could not sail to on account of contrary wind and strong opposing current, wherefore, as well as because they were deprived of drinking water and other provisions, they deemed it good to turn the bow towards Japara, where they arrived yesterday evening and, being provided with the necessary supplies, departed from there and have arrived here today without further incident. Thus done and declared at the head office Samarang, dated as above: [was signed] Gerbrans, Jan Crabbenborg, Swerus Jn. From Java's East Coast, the 2nd of June, 1741. Lee Theunisz, Aug. Bened. Straube, the mark set by Jan Spierenburg and Matthijs Gemeken. [Lower] Indenture [was signed] J. de Haas, First sworn clerk, as expressly commissioned. [Signed] Const. Sibens and P. de Vos.

Demto. den ondercoopman en fiscaal Jeronimus Tonneman Junior wegens in dispositie. Den raad vergadert zijnde wierdende volgende papieren op geleesen te weten Een verclaringe ten overstaan van Javas oost Cust den 2:' Junij 1741. Ja twee gecommitteerde leeden uijt den raad, van Justitie alhier en den fiscaal Jeronimus Recheden morgen gepasseert en gerecolleert Tonneman Junior op gisteren door den assistend en gewesen Joanas resident Johannes Gerbrands, onderchirurgijn Jan Crabbenburg, den quartiermeester sweris Theunisz item de soldaten Augustus Benedictus Straube, Jan Spierenburg, en Matthijs gemeke verder twee brieven door den assistend en Damaks resident urbanus boesijn gesijk, van Eerst gem: datum behelsende tesamen in substantie dat Een „rot der rebelleerende Chineesen van ruijm 1000: koppen op den 23:' bevorens de post Joana hebben aange vallen wanneer den resident aldaar geen nog „ schoot vrij zijnde sijne bijhebbende posthouderen heeft g'ordonneert hun met hem in de daar in gereetheit gezijnde vaartuijgen te embarqueeweest ren en scomp: effecten soo veel als mogelijk was tebergen omme dat Javas oost Cust den 2: Junij 1741. Van onheijl te konnen eschapeeren en den cours narambang tenemen, maar dat den zergeant, Robbert Cammel met 2: corporaals en 6: gemeene zoldaeten nog agterwaren gebleven, de welke den resident heeft vermits contrarie winden Rembang niet konnende aendoen ende Javaanen vande prauwen overboord weg gelopen waren sig met voorsz manschap na herwaarts heeft begeven mitsg:s dat aen hem resident in't minste geen kennis gegeven was door de Jnlanders van de aenkomst
text_translated_detailed: Copy from Java's East Coast, June 2nd, 1741. Saturday, May 27th, 1741. In the morning at nine o'clock. Present: The Commander of this Coast Bartholomeus Visscher, Captain Rudolph Carel von Glan, The Merchant and first administrator Constantijn Sibens, The lieutenant Gerrit Hendrik Alephelt, then under-merchant and second administrator Steven Marcus van der Heyden, the under-merchant and soldier's bookkeeper Pieter de Vos. Likewise, the under-merchant and fiscal Jeronimus Tonneman Junior on account of indisposition. text_translated_detailed: From Java's east coast, under date 2nd June 1741. To the Soesoehoenang PaKoeboeana, residing at Cartasoera. text_translated_detailed: I have the honour to inform Your High Honour with regret that, although many fields have already been harvested and people are still busy with this daily, I have nevertheless, despite my dutiful efforts, not yet been able to complete the harvest, because the Chinese have positioned themselves in the Cadoe between here and Semarang, and according to reports from Java's East Coast under date 4th July 1741, the Javanese are already strong in numbers and increasing daily, so that the rice harvesters, no longer trusting themselves, have all withdrawn. Moreover, just today an Indigo maker from Palnalang, which lies here five miles away, came saying he had been warned by a Chinese that he must retire, so that I have requested the regent there that if the Chinese gather together, even though they do no harm, to keep them under foot, which I hope will meet with Your High Honour's favourable approval. Furthermore, I have the honour to inform Your High Honour that I have placed myself in a good state of defence, and although 2,000 Chinese might wish to attack this fortress, which I nevertheless do not believe, they will accomplish little. Furthermore, I have the honour humbly to request of Your High Honour six sailors, having only three, who are too weak from Java's East Coast, 7th June 1741, to manage the cannon. To His Excellency, the Most Noble, Strict, Great and Esteemed Lord Adriaan Valckenier, Governor-General, and the Well Noble Lords, Councillors of the Netherlands Indies; Most Noble, Strict, Great and Esteemed, Earnest, Valiant, Wise, Provident, Very Generous Lord and Well Noble Gentlemen. From Java's East Coast, dated June 19th, 1741, received on June 21st, 1741. This morning I had the honor to receive your Most Noble, great and esteemed, highly respected letters of the 12th of this month, with six sailors and 3125 rixdollars [modern equivalent: Dutch currency] in Holland double coins, for which I have the honor to express my humble thanks, hoping thereby to be in a position to provide the ship Amsterdam upon its arrival and part of its cargo in rice, and to return that vessel according to your Most Noble, great and esteemed, honored order with the greatest speed. Since I perceive from the circumstances of affairs that my petition for gunpowder from Semarang cannot be well fulfilled, I humbly request through your Most Noble, great and esteemed goodness to be assisted with two thousand pounds per the mardijker [a type of vessel] from Java's East Coast, dated June 19th, 1742, Cupido, which is hereby proceeding, to whom I have given good instructions that in case he should be attacked, he should throw the same overboard, since the sea is unsafe due to various praus [small boats] with Chinese crews, which had gathered together in the Cadoe and had increased according to reports to a thousand.

text_translated_detailed: the Lamadjang from Java's East Coast, dated June 19th, 1741. To His Excellency, the Most Noble Lord Adriaan Valckenier, Governor-General, and the Noble Lords, Councillors of the Netherlands Indies, received June 18th, 1741. Most Noble, Strict, Great and Esteemed, Earnest, Valiant, Wise, Provident, Very Generous, Commanding Lord and Well Noble Gentlemen. Sopantjelt. Following the departure of the most recent respectful letter to Your Most Noble, great and esteemed, dated the 2nd of this month, we have had the esteemed fortune to be honored with their secret missive of the 10th of the most recently passed month of May, brought by the ship Prooftwijk, with which vessel, as also with the Schuijtwijk, there have arrived 150 Baliers [soldiers from Bali] and 160 Buginese [soldiers from Bugis] under their officers, as well as 54 European soldiers from Java's East Coast, dated June 19th, 1741, under the command of Lieutenant Maximilian Constants and Ensign Alexander van Manheijn, who has inspected the quarters here, and everything serving for defense has been brought into readiness, while we respectfully assure that according to human capability everything is being done in these very sorrowful times to destroy or exterminate the ill-disposed Chinese, but the Company's strength now being united is not in a position to reinforce the subordinate trading posts, for to deplete Semarang of personnel would be too much of a risk, while it is still scarcely sufficient against that raging rabble, which has now taken its place of residence on the sugar mill of Captain Que Anko and the so-called Pattijs Bergje, a quarter hour's distance from here, so that Semarang is now sufficiently surrounded by enemies, for the peoples of the chief regent here, Adi Pattij Astrawidjaja, have, according to reports, run away and have from Java's East Coast, dated June 19th, 1741, Jan, the commissioners of the Susuhunan, the beach governors, given sufficient evidence that upon their orders issued to the standing forces, little reliance can be placed.

text_translated_detailed: Translation, containing how the enemy has conducted himself towards Joana. In the continuation hereof, we have the honor to respectfully make known that in accordance with the advices of the commandant Van Velse, the Susuhunan [Pakubuwono II:] of Java's East Coast, under date of the 19th of June 1741, has made known that thousands of Chinese have held themselves upon Java, and that his Majesty through the Ratoe Amancoerat [regent:] together with other well-disposed servants has been moved to tears by the proposition made by the two first ministers to the end of driving out the European servants of this island, and that he disapproves of all this, and that everything at court still seems to be thus. Item, that the Susuhunan has seen fit to dispatch shortly a good number of armed peoples under the command of Tommongong Mankojuda to the land of Cirebon [Ceddoe:] in order to drive out the Chinese who had plotted upon the village of Sarajap [Seriap:] to the number of 600 heads to their places, or if unwilling to massacre them. Meanwhile we have received two letters from the Madurese Pangerang Ade Pattij Tsjacraningraf in the original with their Dutch translations included, concerning that his Excellency requests, as Sumanap of Java's East Coast under date of the 19th of June 1741 and Pamacassan under the obedience of the Company to be able to be, when the Pangerang the great men of Java who carry an unfaithful heart towards the Company undertake to root out, yet that the prince might be strengthened with the aforementioned his younger brothers, sustaining that the rebellious Chinese through God's assistance would also be overcome, further offering 4000 of his subjects for the aforesaid service, provided that from here the necessary pramaijangs [royal decrees:] may be obtained, upon which request we can make no reflection since he is a subject of the prince who through the acceptance of the offered 4000 heads as having occurred outside his order might easily fall into bad sentiments. In the continuation hereof, we have the honor to respectfully make known that in accordance with the advices of the commandant Van Velse, the Susuhunan of Java's East Coast, under date of the 19th of June 1741, has made known that thousands of Chinese have held themselves upon Java, and that his Majesty through the Ratoe Amancoerat together with other well-disposed servants has been moved to tears by the proposition made by the two first ministers to the end of driving out the European servants of this island, and that he disapproves of all this, and that everything at court still seems to be thus. Item, that the Susuhunan has seen fit to dispatch shortly a good number of armed peoples under the command of Tommongong Mankojuda to the land of Cirebon in order to drive out the Chinese who had plotted upon the village of Sarajap to the number of 600 heads to their places, or if unwilling to massacre them. Meanwhile we have received two letters from the Madurese Pangerang Ade Pattij Tsjacraningraf in the original with their Dutch translations included, concerning that his Excellency requests, as Sumanap of Java's East Coast under date of the 19th of June 1741 and Pamacassan under the obedience of the Company to be able to be, when the Pangerang the great men of Java who carry an unfaithful heart towards the Company undertake to root out, yet that the prince might be strengthened with the aforementioned his younger brothers, sustaining that the rebellious Chinese through God's assistance would also be overcome, further offering 4000 of his subjects for the aforesaid service, provided that from here the necessary pramaijangs may be obtained, upon which request we can make no reflection since he is a subject of the prince who through the acceptance of the offered 4000 heads as having occurred outside his order might easily fall into bad sentiments. text_translated_detailed: Java's East Coast received on June 19, 1741. — I humbly beseech Your Excellency's assistance so that I may be as Sumanap in Pamacassan under the obedience of the Company, for I can no longer manage well under the Javanese, nor can my family from Java's East Coast under the date of June 19, 1741, neither young nor old, because the great ones of Java have no affection for Madura, unless Your Excellency helps me or the Company has affection for Madura, then I with my whole family from Madura shall certainly be ruined. It would be most welcome to me if the Esteemed Company or Your Excellency would be pleased to employ me together with Sumanap and Pamacassan, and when the great ones of Java might harbor ill will against the Company, I promise to drive them out, as soon as I have received orders from the Esteemed Company, strengthened with the Sumanap and Pamacassans, and the common people of Java, I believe, if I but give a sign, would all come over to me if I were equal with Sumanap and Pamacassan. What then would have happened on Java under a captain of the Company who was merely a commissioner, there would have been no difficulty, as little as with the Chinese, but I do not know it rightly, God is almighty. If the Esteemed Company would but be pleased to take me under obedience from Java's East Coast under the date of June 19, 1747, and Your Excellency would be pleased to support me regarding my wife, for that is Madoeratna, that is no trouble, such is not unknown to Your Excellency, all that I have to say is contained in this letter. The council being convened and seated, there was resumed the esteemed missive of Their High Excellencies from the 26th of the previous month, containing among other things the granted qualification to be able to publish an act of amnesty in order to be able to free the good Chinese from any harmful encounters, and against that to drive out the ill-intentioned ones more easily, with the stipulation that the term of the amnesty would be set at one month after its publication, and of the same no other Chinese would be allowed to profit than those residing on Java and such as have betaken themselves there before or at the beginning of the revolt of Batavia. text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast dated June 19th, 1741. / Agreed [signed] J. de Haas, E. clerk. Copy. Rembang. To the under-merchant Zacharias de Bensin, resident there; Title. In response to Your Excellency's letter of the 4th instant, it serves that we at present cannot provide you with the requested weapons and gunpowder until we ourselves are provisioned therewith, and meanwhile we make known that the Susuhunan has dispatched a number of armed soldiers under the command of the beach regents of Tuban, Caliwongoe, Kandal, and Grobogan in order to destroy the rebellious Chinese rabble and cleanse the land of such vermin. Meanwhile, enclosed herewith is the requested act of salary increase for Sergeant Jankuyser, which can be handed to him from Java's East Coast under date of June 19th, 1741, while remaining under our authority. [undersigned] Your Excellency's good friends [signed]. D. Visscher, R.C. von Glan, Const. Sibens, G.t h. Alexhelt, S.m. V.n d. Heyden, P. de Vos, and J. Tonneman Junior. [in margin]: Samarang, May 9th, 1741. L. Baeren [undersigned] Agreed, J. Clouw, secretary, Copy. Rembang; To the under-merchant Zacharias de Bensin, resident there. Title. Meanwhile, enclosed herewith is the requested act of salary increase for Sergeant Jankuyser, which can be handed to him from Java's East Coast under date of June 19th, 1741, while remaining under our authority. undersigned Your Excellency's good friends signed. D. Visscher, R.C. von Glan, Const. Sibens, G.t h. Alexhelt, S.m. V.n d. Heyden, P. de Vos, and J. Tonneman Junior. in margin: Samarang, May 9th, 1741. L. Baeren undersigned Agreed, J. Clouw, secretary, Copy. Rembang; To the under-merchant Zacharias de Bensin, resident there. Title. Your Excellency's letter of the 31st of the past month we have received and from it with satisfaction seen Your Excellency's disposition concerning the 72 natives taken into service and together with a gathered Goanese capper force serving to protect Your Excellency's post, we shall not be lacking in recruiting you from Java's East Coast under date of June 19th, 1741, as soon as relief from Batavia arrives, which is expected daily. text_translated_detailed: June 1741 [undersigned] Agreed, J. de Haas, E.g. clerk [signed] From Java's East Coast under date of June 19th, 1741. Copy. Samarang. To the Esteemed and Honored Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, E. chief merchant and governor of Java's northeast coast. Title. My reference to my previous [letter] of May 31st last past, I make known to Your Esteemed and Honored Excellency that the rebels have gathered at Lassum and Padjancongan; the principal leaders are at Lassum: The Sianko, Liliamko, both from Cassum, Koe Sionko, former Sabandhar here, and Li-sweeko from Bouton. At Padjancongan: Tsi-sjoeko, Sabandhar to Paradessje, Ian Linko from Coelij, and Lim Keijko from Padjancongan. The Javanese regents are gathering from Java's East Coast under date of June 19th, 1741, their forces without one being able to discern to what end. Here also, as one hears, those from Tanjong who had been at Joana have departed. One also hears murmuring among the Javanese that the head of these rebels would be the lieutenant Que Jonko at the Coast, and that he had brewed this with some Javanese. To the esteemed Governor. I have not wished to let this opportunity pass without making known to Your Esteemed and Honored Excellency the above-mentioned, wherewith I abbreviate and remain with respect [undersigned] Title [below] Your Esteemed and Honored Excellency's obedient and obedient servant [was signed] L. d' Bensin. text_translated_detailed: 1741 [undersigned] Agreed, anno J. de Haas: E.g. clerk, signed. From Java's East Coast under date of June 19th, 1741. Samarang. To the Esteemed and Honored Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, chief merchant and governor of Java's northeast coast, together with the council there. Title. This serves to make known to Your Esteemed and Honored Excellency that the rebels, pressing us ever more closely, have advanced from Lassum to Jamplong, half a mile from here. The regents of Lassum and Padjancongan, who have returned from Cartasoera, have had read to me a commission from the realm's administrator to Cartasoera, which states that they were ordered to return hither in order to make the rebellious Chinese here from Java's East Coast under date of June 19th, 1741, submit to the Emperor and the Esteemed Company. In which case the Emperor will stand by them, and otherwise they would be declared as enemies of the said Emperor. Whereupon I requested them to cause the said rebels to each return to their dwelling places. They promise to do so if it is possible. I have further requested them, in case of refusal, to use force against them, which they, the regents, say they must first bring to their people's attention, which makes me see that they cannot be relied upon, for their people are at hand. We are here not in a state to undertake the least thing for our defense. From Java's East Coast under date of June 19th, 1741, if we cannot rely upon the so-called Macassarese, which I greatly doubt. Last night we were under arms the entire night and have, to all appearances, nothing better to expect. In sum, our state is as bad as one could imagine, for if

text_translated_detailed: To notify Your Excellency that presently around 50 vessels full of Chinese are anchored outside the river of Sedoenang [Semarang], waiting very probably from Java's East Coast under Date 19 June 1741, for another wind in order to come this way, for towards the east it is against the wind, which is why Your Excellency is requested for reinforcement, for against such a multitude of Chinese it would be impossible to resist: in the hope that Your Excellency will be pleased to give this matter favorable consideration, I remain with the utmost submission [undersigned] Title [lower]: Your Excellency's most obedient servant [was signed] U.s Bresijn [in margin:] Qualladamak the 9th June 1741. Per S. Clercq.

After customary preamble, I bring to Your Excellency's knowledge that the residence of the resident here, the guard of the soldiers, the house of the sergeant, and everything that stood there by order of the Chinese has been knocked down by the Javanese and carried away, and distributed as plunder to each person, and the warehouse they have relocated west of the post, which serves as their guard post, where daily sometimes 40, sometimes 30 men keep watch, though all the parnackans [uncertain: possibly a rank or group] who are Mohammedans have left from here and have always been with the enemy. text_translated_detailed: From Javanese affairs, dated 20 June 1741. Copy. To the Pangerang Ingabij Looring Passier, at Kartasura, After customary preliminaries, I hereby make known to you, my brother, that through various letters I have requested assistance from the Susuhunan for the destruction of the ill-disposed Chinese, which has also been done through two letters from their High Excellencies, and His Majesty has indeed already issued orders for this, and also sent his coastal governors to the end that we might consult with them and provide proper assistance; they have shown evidence of this to the extent that the enemies have passed freely and now lie scattered all around Semarang and have for the most part laid it in ashes, although the Company's peoples have been helpers to the coastal dwellers, the first mentioned of the last having been abandoned, whereby we were forced, from Javanese affairs, dated 20 June 1744, to retire with loss to the lodge, after which I requested those governors in the friendliest manner to assist the head office, but they are nowhere to be found; what shall I now say to you, my brother? It is a well-known matter that the Chinese nation has for some years schemed a betrayal to destroy the Company and afterward to make themselves masters of the Javanese realm, when certainly His Majesty will find that it cannot exist without the Company, for that rabble has merely been driven out by their evil deeds from their own land and by His Majesty's regents permitted to settle themselves throughout all of Java, and thus to the utmost they will strive to carry out their objective. That his governors and the Majesty's coastal regents are so cowardly or not properly disposed is certainly through the instigation of some of his, from Javanese affairs, dated 20 June 1741.

Den 2:' courant hebben wij perder Zergeant Jan herman better en 2: soldaaten ons Jongst Eerbiedig schrijven tot uw Ed:e agtb: g'expedieert; en den 11:' daar aan bij retour van den sergeant Pieter van hekelen en 2: gemeene militairen wierden wij verEerd d' mst uw Ed: agtb: veel gerespecteerde brief gedagteekend 3: tevooren, waar op in reverentelijk antwoord dient, dat kort voor den ontfangst van uw Ed:e agtb welgemelte missive, den chinees sabandhaar que Pouko, sig van sibaijoe g'absenteert had, en men na alle gedane omsoekinge, nog niet kan te weten komen waar na toe, weshalven Van Javas :t Cust oder dato 20:' Junij 1741. / de goederen die alhier van hem mogten gevonden werden in beslag sullen genomen en daarmede gelijk als met die van andere scomp: fugatieve onderdanen na de ordre gehandelt werden; ook dat hier niemand onder benamingen van Loe Tjanko of Sitjenko door u Ed: agtbare mede gerequireerd bekend is voorts betuijgt den zergeant Emanuelt Lubregt schade submisse dankbaarheijt aan uwEd:e agtb:, voor de verleende permissie om te mogen trouwen met de Christen dogter Maria Pieters: van batavia En soo doet, ook den timmerman Milchior Thomasz: voor dat na Costij mag komen ten Eijnde sijnde verlossinge t' obtineeren, en wij voor dat uEd: agtb: ons bij nadere occagie met een andere van dat ambagt voor, „sien zal, denselven heeft nog Eenig onderhandig werk, en zal deehe lroe daarmede gedaan hebbende bij Eerste gelegentheijd volgen; Van Javas:t Cust onder Dato 20:' Junij 1741. ondertusschen communiceeren wij uEd: agtb: dat den Jntier gen:t Noraens van Madras als mattroos bescheijden geweestt op d' alhier sijnde Engels chialoup de sorean
text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast under Date 20th June 1741: Copy Semarang. To the Esteemed and Honorable Mister Bartholomeus Visscher, chief merchant and governor of Java's Northeast Coast together with the council there; — Title. On the 2nd of the current month we sent Sergeant Jan Herman Better and 2 soldiers our most recent humble letter to your Esteemed Honor, dispatched; and on the 11th thereafter by return of Sergeant Pieter van Hekelen and 2 common soldiers we were honored with your Esteemed Honor's much respected letter dated the 3rd before, to which in reverent answer it must be said that shortly before the receipt of your Esteemed Honor's aforementioned missive, the Chinese merchant Sabandhaar que Pouko had absented himself from Sibaijoe, and after all inquiries made, one still cannot ascertain where to, for which reason. From Java's East Coast under Date 20th June 1741, the goods that might be found here from him shall be seized and shall be handled with them just as with those of other Company fugitive subjects according to orders; also that here no one under the names of Loe Tjanko or Sitjenko is known as required by your Esteemed Honor. Furthermore, Sergeant Emanuel Lubregt expresses humble submission and gratitude to your Esteemed Honor for the granted permission to marry the Christian daughter Maria Pieters of Batavia. And so also does the carpenter Melchior Thomasz for being able to come to the coast in order to obtain his discharge, and we [request] that your Esteemed Honor will provide us on a later occasion with another of that trade, the same one still has some outstanding work, and will have completed it and will follow at the first opportunity; From Java's East Coast under Date 20th June 1741, meanwhile we communicate to your Esteemed Honor that the entire soldier Noraens from Madras as a sailor was on duty on the English sloop here called the Sorean

Meanwhile, we consider it our utmost duty to bring to your Excellencies' attention that the Pangerang Adipati Tjacraningaat informed the first undersigned yesterday that seven days ago, all the Chinese inhabitants of the village of Djambong have departed to Lasem in order to join with the rebelling Chinese who have overrun the Company's trading post, and thus also to attack Rembang; and at the same time offered troops either under his son Sorradeningaat or in his own person to act against them. text_translated_detailed: Received: the 6th of July, 1741. From Java's east coast. The 2nd of July, Anno 1741. Most Esteemed, Strict, and Greatly Respected Gentlemen. text_translated_detailed: From the sailor Van Javas, East Coast, 2nd July 1741, Batavia; To His Excellency the High and Noble Lord Adriaan Valckenier, Governor-General and the Noble Lords Councillors of the Dutch Indies; High and Noble, Stern, Most Esteemed, Earnest, Mighty, Wise, Provident, Most Generous, Far-Ruling Lord and Well-Noble Lords. — Albertus van Sandbergen, having been compelled by numerous pressing matters in these dangerous times on Java to leave unanswered until now certain points from your High Excellency's greatly esteemed missives dated 14th April, 16th and 26th May, and 7th of the month just passed, we now have the honour, being obligated thereupon, to serve that the sent monies with the yacht Catharina Sophia and the ships Proostwijk and Schuijtwijk, as well as gunpowder, have been properly delivered, for which favourable arrangement we express our deepest thanks, just as the first undersigned thanks your High Excellency for having been pleased to honour him with the Van Javas, East Coast, 2nd July, Year 1741.— No. 7. text_translated_detailed: From Java's South Coast, the 2nd of July 1741. Extract of Resolution taken in the Council of Policy at the head office Samarang; on Saturday the 10th of June in the year 1741. The council being convened and seated, there was reviewed their High Excellencies' esteemed missive of the 26th of the previous month, containing among other things the granted qualification to be able to publish an act of amnesty in order to be able to free the good Chinese from any harmful encounters, and against this the evil-minded [Chinese] the more easily to be driven out with the stipulation that the term of the amnesty should be set at one month after its publication, and of the same no other Chinese should be allowed to profit than those who dwell on Java, which are peaceful and such [Chinese] before or at the beginning of the revolt of Batavia have moved toward [the Company], over which point in council it was deliberated whether the aforementioned act should proceed now or not, and finally unanimously decided that this publication shall remain suspended until the enemy Chinese are defeated, since it is to be maintained that under the raging conspiracy no good people are to be found, all the more so since it is thought that they have had sufficient time to separate themselves from the bad [elements]. Samarang in Council, dated Visscher, R. C. von Dus, S. Cont. Sibens, S. M. v. d. Glan, Heijden, P. D'vos, and J. Tonneman Auditor. Agreed, BaerenClouw, secretary. From Java's South Coast, under date the 2nd of July 1741, to the Esteemed and Honorable Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, Commander on and along Java's South Coast at Samarang, received the 26th of June in the year 1741. After customary preamble, Brother, I bring to your Excellency's knowledge that there are many both coastal and inland Javanese who have offered themselves to me to come to the Company's aid, under the condition of remaining to dwell in their places, provided that when it is required of me to carry out my command, regarding which I request your Excellency's advice, for my and their people's utmost desire is to be able to know your Excellency's judgment thereupon, which my understanding [prompts me] to present to your Excellency. Furthermore, it is brought to your knowledge from Java's South Coast under date the 2nd of July 1741 that at Tuban they have found a conspiracy of approximately 400 Chinese, all armed, bearing two flags, and clothed in red jackets, and also that those of that nation who are at Gresik are ready for battle, and these same are also treated very kindly by the Javanese.

text_translated_detailed: Java's East Coast under Date 2nd July 1741. / Western strand governor the adipati Djajadining goes to the Honorable and esteemed Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, Commander on and along Java's northeast coast until Semarang, received the 30th June 1741. After customary preamble; Your Honored letter has been well delivered to me, from which I learned with sorrow that Your Honored self holds me suspect of a betrayal with the Chinese schemed against the Prince and the Company, to which I am completely innocent. That evening when Your Honored self summoned me and Tjitrasoema to the lodge and ordered us to request more people from the Susuhunang, this was immediately carried out by us, and Your Honored self advised closing the great gate at the house of the Chinese captain from outside, and to break down the high bridge in order to prevent the Chinese who found themselves inside the patjinan from having an exit. But Your Honored self postponed this until the following day, when I waited the entire morning until eleven o'clock, when I learned that the aforementioned Chinese were in great upheaval, and through one of the people who had been sent to me at the sugar mill, I was informed that that nation had raised some flags there. I found myself partly as completely abandoned by all my companions and some subjects, which fear has caused me to abandon. text_translated_detailed: esteemed Lord Bartholomeus Visscher Commander on and along Java's North East Coast at Semarang received on the 28th of June 1741. Now, customary preamble Since that Your Excellency has been pleased to command me and the Adipati DjaJadiningaat to come to you, so it serves for Your Excellency's information that I have given notice of this at the court or to the Patti Notta Coesoema of Java's East Coast under Date 2nd July 1741, while requesting to be able to be assisted by the Radeen Tommongong of Siedajoe the tommongong of Grisee and the Ingabeij of Lamongan Concerning my departure from Semarang has been caused by the fact that in the morning there appeared to me an emissary of the Adipati Djajadiningaat who came to inform me that his master had been requested by the Semarang head regent to go with him from his encampment, for which reason I also set myself on the way to Caliegowe where on the following day there came to me an emissary of Your Excellency to call me as well as to show me where Djajadiningaat was staying who having been brought to Siwalan I did not find the aforementioned Djajaningrat but was told that he was at Pangaron after which I wished to proceed to Your Excellency, but was, by the hostile Chinese of Talahab in my fore— of Java's East Coast under date 2nd July 1741 taken aground and through fear driven back, as when Your Excellency's emissary accompanied by one of my mantries went home, truly I was very grieved when I saw myself abandoned by Your Excellency. The reason that I have absented myself from Semarang is to be attributed solely to Astrawidjaja, because he left his entrusted land and Djajaningrat his dwelling to the advantage of the enemies which caused me to fear remaining alone at Semarang. All this I submit to Your Excellency's wise judgment Finally the bearer of this takes soetawasa for Your Excellency along with some chickens

text_translated_detailed:
First, to be sent there with the yacht Christina Sophia: 12 baliers [Balinese soldiers], 12 Buginese with their under-officers, 36 snaphaances [muskets], 500 pounds of gunpowder and lead, furthermore 6 loads of rice. Finally, the resident must be notified of this by letter this very evening, just as it is ordered that he and the garrison, if they can offer no further resistance, shall endeavor to save themselves on the aforementioned small yacht from Java's south coast under date 2nd July 1741. In the meantime, the loading of the yacht Christina Sophia destined for Rembang is further understood to be transported in the ship Schuijtwijk, except for these loads of rice previously destined for the Samarang office [uncertain: "comtoir gedestineerd"]. In council, date as above, signed: R. Visscher, R.C. von Glan, Const. Bu., Const. Sibens, G.t K. Alephelt, S.n M.s V.n d.r Heijden, P.r de Vos Baeren Clouw. Agreed, signed: P. L. Baeren Clouw, secretary's copy.

To the under-merchant Zacharias de Bensin, Resident and council there.

Title: With sorrow we have seen from your letter of the 27th of this month the poor condition of the Rembang office regarding the raging Chinese against whom you request assistance with manpower. And since we here lack everything, we can for this time help you no more than with 12 Buginese, 12 baliers with their under-officers, 500 pounds of gunpowder, 36 muskets and lead, as well as 6 loads of rice. The small yacht Christina Sophia brings all of this. However, if you cannot offer further resistance against the enemy, you shall endeavor to retire with the small garrison in the yacht that is there to us here. In the meantime, we commend the Company's interests to divine protection and remain with great greetings your good friends. Thus Visscher, R.a C.s

Report made to the Esteemed and Honorable Bartholomeus Visscher, Commander on and along Java's south coast, by the under-steersman on the yacht the Young Philip, Arnoud Danielsz.

The reporter states that he yesterday toward evening arrived here at the roadstead with the aforementioned yacht from Rembang on account of the power of the Chinese rebels as well as through lack of provisions, which small vessel at the roadstead of the aforementioned Residency had driven, and that on the 23rd of the recently passed month he sent the boat to shore from Java's south coast under date 2nd July 1741, with some empty casks in order to have them filled with water. However, in the meantime, when that water was being carried from the lodge to the shore, a great number of armed Chinese suddenly appeared there, striking drums and blowing trumpets, whereby the water-carrying persons were forced to abandon the casks and some returned to the lodge as well as the boat, thus leaving the aforementioned casks as prey to the rebels, who struck them all to pieces, notwithstanding that many shots were fired both from the lodge

Resolution taken in Council on the first of July 1741. All present.

The council being gathered and seated, there was taken into consideration the request made by the captain of the Buginese here, Jntje Boejong, to be permitted to transport the body of the Soudas Turk Achemet Lebe, who died in his house, and his surviving male slaves to Batavia. I have the honor to assure you that the assistance rendered by Your Excellency in these times shall be rewarded not only with a due gratitude but principally with such recognition that Your Excellency, my brother, and your well-disposed family shall at all times be able to say that the Company's welfare is attached to you, and everything shall be done to give Your Excellency, my brother, complete satisfaction. Be therefore a good, amiable, and well-disposed person, of which sufficient proof has been given before, who does not give his heart as a prize to enemies who deceive their own master, but rather to the welfare of the general good of Java's East Coast under date of the 2nd of July 1741. All that I have to say for this time is contained in this letter, which is written at the head comptoir Samarang on the 1st of July

text_translated_detailed: to communicate that the Chinese and Javanese aforementioned have seized control of the pangong [fortified structure] at the seaside of the well-esteemed Lord Den L Van Javasot Cust [Java Southeast Coast] under date 4th July 1741, extraordinary council member Nicolaas Crul, here stationed at Caligare, and have provided themselves there with bastions in order to become masters of the seashore, whereby communication with the ships and all supplies can be prevented. On the other side, over the southern road of the houses of the lieutenant que gonko, Depattij Djajadiningaat, and the passageway, they have also fortified themselves with nothing but earthen and wooden palisades, and thus we are now so constrained and shall have to suffer from the lack of everything until the water runs out; of which there is already scarcity due to this garrison, and even more for the ships since the enemy blocks the river from above. We fear that we shall be unable to preserve Samarang after the lapse of one month, so with regard to the Van Javasot Cust of 4th July 1741 aforementioned, as well as the mortality among the Europeans and natives due to hardships is consuming the small force, which is also diminished by daily attacks against the enemy. These circumstances, your high and esteemed lordship, we beseech you to take into consideration, as they threaten us with total destruction. Here there are no native vessels, and even less Javanese who can command them. Therefore we take the liberty to say that if we are not assisted with the greatest speed with 2 to 3,000 Europeans and loyal natives, as well as with the fulfillment of the attached copy of the requisition, we shall not be able to inflict damage upon the Chinese and allied Javanese, and even less be able to destroy them. Thus we humbly beseech the necessary assistance. How matters stand at Passourouang can be seen from the attached copy of the letter given by the commandant Siersma and

text_translated_detailed: Van Javasot Cust [Java Southeast Coast] under date 4th July 1741. Copy. Samarang. To the esteemed and honorable Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, chief merchant and governor of all Java, No. O.t Cust [Southeast Coast], together with the Council there. Upon your high and respected letters, free of your esteemed lordship, sub. date 16th August, which reached us on the 23rd thereof at Surabaya, we have done everything within our power that in such dangerous times and circumstances is useful and necessary. And notwithstanding the Javanese under this unhappy conduct of the rebellious and bloodthirsty rabble, as we have understood with sorrow from the Chinese through your esteemed lordship's many honored missives, the first undersigned, under the favorable and kind consideration of your esteemed lordship, has deemed it necessary to attempt to speak with the native regents here and in the surrounding area, without however saying the least thing about one matter or another, except that the first undersigned did not doubt that they would keep good watch in their entrusted district and give him immediate notice of any occurrence, which they have also promised. However, in conversation with the ingabeij [native official] of Bangel among others, he assured us that the Radeen Adepattij Nattacoesoema at Cartasoera had incited the Chinese rabble and the emperor had taken this very ill. However, they added that the Soesoekang is young, and whatever this realm's administrator brings forth or says is all approved by the aforementioned Soesoehoenang. The first undersigned has tried, with a fair opportunity, to discover even more regarding this matter, but he said he knew nothing else than that some native chiefs, who were held at court, Van Javasot Cust under date 4th July 1741, who were inclined toward the Company, and could submit themselves there, as Sumanap and Pamacassan had done in former times, namely the Radeen Tommangorg of Sidaija, the Tommagong of Grissee, the

The first undersigned has tried, with a fair opportunity, to discover even more regarding this matter, but he said he knew nothing else than that some native chiefs, who were held at court, Van Javasot Cust under date 4th July 1741, who were inclined toward the Company, and could submit themselves there, as Sumanap and Pamacassan had done in former times, namely the Radeen Tommangorg of Sidaija, the Tommagong of Grissee, the Ingaleij Kanon also at Grissee, and the Ingabeij of Lamongong. What is known to your esteemed lordship regarding this, we are aware, but we have deemed it our utmost duty to necessarily communicate such important matters to your esteemed lordship. Furthermore, we take the liberty once more in all subordination to humbly beseech your esteemed lordship to be permitted to obtain such goods as lying on the attached copy of a requisition, as we have had the honor, besides our most recent submissive writing of the 21st August, to dispatch to your esteemed lordship by the sailor Dirk van Heijnsbergen, since we have here only 1,000 pounds of gunpowder and 200 pounds of lead bullets remaining, and also to obtain a good reinforcement of soldiers and 100 pieces of snaphaances [muskets], in order to be properly in a state to make good resistance. From there came the sorrowful and weeping missionaries, struck down with grief, and answered that they had been sent from the chief to Surabaya to bring the Company's letter to Rembang. Whereupon the bloodthirsty wicked creatures began to attack them and beat them miserably with sticks, and the returned Jappa Doeko received such a heavy and merciless blow on the left side of his head that blood followed thereafter, so that he had to retreat to his vessel and abandoned his companion without knowing at that time whether he was alive or dead. However, after much difficulty, on the first of this month he arrived here. So on the same day by the undersigned, two Javanese, Jiveo Mongolo and Tsitra Juda, subordinates of the Radeen in Ingabeij here, the aforementioned Your Honored Lordship's letter was sent back to the Java South Coast, under Date 12th July 1747. From there no answer has yet been received. Subsequently, we received on the 23rd of the same month from the returned Sergeant Jan Herman Bitter and two soldiers, Your Honored Lordship's esteemed letter of the 18th previous, as well as an Extract letter.

text_translated_detailed: the Dutch Indies have been pleased to honour Your Honour with the position of Commandeur of this quality from Java's East Coast under date 12th July 1741, with which honourable charge we have the honour to congratulate Your Honour, and in the writing of letters and otherwise we shall regulate ourselves accordingly.
