After customary preamble. By return of my emissary, from Java's East Coast under Date 12th July 1741, I was honored with Your Esteemed's letter, whose contents I have understood. I do not doubt that the Company can well perceive how matters stand with the Susuhunan, of which I do not know what I shall say. Be assured, however, that I shall not assist the prince in anything against the Company, but shall always follow Your Esteemed's counsel. I greatly desire to be released from the Emperor and to be brought under the authority of the Company, for which reason I request that Your Esteemed be pleased to release me by written document, for I do not know what I am to do, so long as I continue thus, for I dare not come to Your Esteemed without special permission from the prince, or must fear his displeasure. I request that after obtaining what is stated above, the Javanese who are inclined to follow me, together with those of Sumanap and Pamacassan, may be my traveling companions for the peace of mind of my subjects. text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast under date 12th July 1741. Copy and Translation: Javanese missive addressed to the Esteemed and Honorable Mister Bartholomeus Visscher, Commander on and along Java's Northeast Coast, by the Eastern Strand Governor Adipattij Tsitra Soema, received on the 9th of July 1741. After the customary preamble: Your Esteemed missive has reached me well, in which Your Esteemed self has been pleased to correct me regarding my faults, which I accept with thanks, for who else would instruct me but Your Esteemed self? I acknowledge that I did not act rightly in leaving Samarang, which was sent to me by the prince there. This was caused by the fact that the Adipattij Djajaningrat requested me to go with him, and Adipattij Astrawidjaja made me afraid. Moreover, the translator informed me that when I was called by Your Esteemed self, I should not come from Java's East Coast under date 12th July 1741, for I would certainly be taken into custody, which I did not initially consider, but when he told me this for the third time, I answered him: why would I be taken into custody, for I do not know that any wrongdoing has been found in me? Your Esteemed self commands me once more to come to Your Esteemed self, which has also been ordered to me by the Susuhunang, in order to be able to consult with Your Esteemed self. However, having spoken with the Adipattij Djajaningrat Soeralaja Soerenggrana and all the regents, they say that they do not dare to do this, since the Chinese hold all the passages, so that if it lasts any longer, I shall betake myself to Japara. Furthermore, I make known to Your Esteemed self that the letter to the commandant at Cartasoera has been delivered by one of my subordinates. Undersigned. Translated by me. It was signed P.s Vlsueur, by Translator. Undersigned. From Java's East Coast under date 12th July 1791. Accordeert. Signed. P. L. Baeren Clouw, secretary. Copy and Translation.

Javanese missive addressed by the Eastern Strand Governor Adipattij Tsitra Soema to the under-merchant Lambert Depeltak, resident on behalf of the Company, and the Lieutenant Reijnier Engelink at Japara in Samarang, received on the 9th of July 1791. After the customary preamble: My departure from Samarang was caused by the fact that the Adipattij Djajaningrat abandoned his encampment and Astrawidjaja abandoned his entrusted land, fleeing to Siwalan. Therefore, I betook myself to Coligaie, where in the morning there appeared before me envoys of the Esteemed and Honorable Mister the Commander, to summon me and to request me, from Java's East Coast under date 12th July 1741, that I would show him where Djaja Ningrat was being held. When we came to the aforementioned Siwalan, it was said that he had betaken himself with Astrawidjaja to Pangadat. Then I wanted to betake myself to the Esteemed and Honorable Mister, but was met by the Chinese who came from Talakap, who through fear made me turn back, and the aforementioned envoy and also a mantri [local official] departed. Truly, when I saw myself hidden from the Company, I was very confused, requesting that Your Esteemed self be pleased to send the bearer of this forward with a letter to Samarang. Undersigned. Translated by me. It was signed P.s Sesueua, by Translator. Undersigned. Accordeert. Signed. P. L. Haerenclouw, secretary. Copy and Translation. Javanese missive by the Eastern Strand Governor.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's Outgoing Customs, dated 12th July 1741. / Translator of the undersigned Agrees / [with] Baaren Clouw, secretary's Copy. / Monday, the 10th July in the year 1741, in the morning at 9 o'clock, all present, through the inland burgher sergeant Carel Carelsz and further burghers here, presented to this council was a request containing that, since on the 26th of the recently passed month of June in the attack against the hostile Chinese, they were also drawn out and that they, during that time, both by day and by night in full arms have patrolled positively in the service of the Honored Company, while enjoying cost money and rations, they wished to be accepted. So it is that the request, for further reasons, by Java's Customs, dated 12th July 1741. From the said request, not only was it judged fair and proper, but also to encourage them, unanimously it was resolved to consent thereto, and moreover the aforementioned sergeant Carelsz, as being of good conduct, to promote to ensign [vaandrig: a junior officer rank] for the said Company, which according to the name roll consists of 5 sergeants, 6 corporals, and 30 soldiers, though all subject to the approval of their High Excellencies. Samarang in Council, dated as before: [with signatures:] Wasvisscher, R.C. von Glanget, Constantijn Sibens, G.t H.k, Alepheer, C.n v. der Heyden, Pr. de Vos, Ms. E. Tonneman Junior, and P.r L.L. Furthermore, we humbly make known that the Madurese Pangerang Ade Pattij Tsjacraningaat has communicated by two letters from Java's West Coast, dated 19th July 1741, that his Excellency was summoned by the Susuhunan to proceed armed to Cartasoera, that a Ratoe Amancoerat, his Excellency's relative, together with family was expected there, likewise that the aforementioned prince had 400 Chinese put to death, those who had been living in Madura, whereupon in answer it was served that all that which could tend to the encouragement of that prince, to remain steadfast in the preservation of the general good, to which conclusion to proceed, certainly the prince was moved, since it was securely reported that the Chinese there had attempted to betray him. The aforementioned patriarch has been asked in a further letter to persist in his customary goodwill toward the alliance, with no further circumstances extended therein. The former captain of the Chinese nation here, Que Anko, having died in the Company's service and in chains, his body was, according to council resolution, thrown into the river by the justice officers. This having been brought thus far into account, the treacherous Chinese attacked from early morning along the pass and around Samarang, and finally at the Chinese quarter, whereby they initially became master of it, but were afterward driven back to the pass. Since this had been prepared thus far, the court messengers Wieradjaja and Tirta Wigoena came in the name of the ruler to inform the commandant van Velse that the two envoys who had served to deliver the ruler's letter to the Madurese prince depattij Tsjacramigaat are here, and that they have returned. They obtained no audience from the prince, but received the letter at the gate of the prince's residence by one of his officials, when the aforementioned envoys, on the order of the pangerang, immediately had to depart from the island of Madura from Java's east coast under date of July 19, 1741, without a letter of greeting to the ruler or being permitted to rest and provision themselves on Madura. Wherefore the realm's administrator was summoned by his majesty and subsequently it was decided that the two regents of Grisee from Salatiga shall be recalled from here to return to their residences, in order to guard the same against any evil intentions of the Madurese prince, and in place of the aforementioned grisee officials shall depart to Salatiga the tommongong [regional military commander], Djaja Soederga, who shall also take with him some cannon pieces, but one does not know for certain the day of his departure (understood) Agrees (certified) P.r L Haeren Clouw, secretary. Samarang; To the Honorable and Esteemed Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, Commander on and along Java's North East Coast, together with the Council there. — Dstut. — : Our most recent subordinate letters to your Honorable and Esteemed [address], Sergeant Hendrik van Alst and the soldiers Michiel Lodewijk Woltman and Jan Ballier, dispatched on the 4th of this month, per pramajang, to which we have conducted ourselves with reverence ever since. text_translated_detailed: fired with cannons and muskets, but by God's goodness without wounding any of us. With the breaking of dawn, we saw that they had brought three machines, two of which were made of beams and buffalo hides running on wheels, from Java's southeast coast. On the 28th of July 1741, up to a musket shot's distance from this fortress, behind which several hundreds held themselves very still, while the others descended with great noise, certainly to draw us out. But through constant cannon fire, we finally drove them to flight from that machine, leaving two dead behind. Also in various places we have found blood, so that we do not doubt that some of them have been killed and wounded. Where they now are or what they are doing, I cannot ascertain, so that we scarcely dare open the gate. The 23 Europeans that I still lack, together with the inland militia, have not yet arrived. Whether the passage is blocked for them or not, I do not know. But I find myself obliged to inform your High Excellency of our weakened state and humbly to request all possible assistance, since it could well happen that the Chinese who are gathering at Java's southeast coast at Marang and elsewhere might come down here if they are made afraid, especially if the Prince of Madura comes to Java, whom, as I understand, has undertaken to relieve Rembang. Also I have discovered that our palisading, notwithstanding that it has not stood long, is in a poor state, being mostly rotted, so that I have had to prop and brace it in many places. text_translated_detailed: for the disposition of your High Excellency, and since the seafarers of the ships lying here at the roadstead were murmuring and making claims regarding the aforementioned chialoup, asserting that they had become master of a great prize thereof from the hands of their enemies the Chinese, and that in such a manner they did not wish to expose themselves to such dangers on the 31st of July 1741, to satisfy them we deemed it good to expand the instruction previously granted to the ship's officers insofar as all Chinese coming here at the roadstead with indigenous vessels, instead of being sent here, shall remain on the ships under secure custody until further orders. Finally, that all Chinese unwilling to show their passes or otherwise resist shall be massacred, to be seen in more detail in the enclosed copy of the letter to the ship's officers and resolutions taken in council on the 20th and 21st of this month. Finally, this serves as an accompaniment to a sealed box with particular letters brought from Macassar per the Chinese chialoup on the 31st of July 1741, and with whom, together with ten of his Agto Juragan [uncertain: possibly a title or rank] mates coming here in the river, had to undergo an unexpected massacre by the fury of the common people, with which we remain with due and deep respect. The Relator [person giving the report] now ten days ago with a Company letter to the commandant Johannes van Velse, [traveling] from Carisuera [Kartasura] from here and [being] dispatched as advisor, says that he arrived seven days after the date, namely the last Saturday that passed, at Wonogarang, and there encountered the Javanese named Marta Proena who, upon inquiry, the relator reported had been sent by his known master Radeen Depati Natta-Kusuma in order to deliver two letters here at Semarang, one to the Tumenggung Manka Judo, head of the Cadre, and the other to the former captain of the Chinese nation here, Que Anko. After which report the relator informed himself about the situation at Kartasura through the said messenger, [and] learned that on Thursday before, or the 19th of this month in the morning at approximately eight o'clock, the Susuhunan [Javanese ruler] had sent some money to the From Java's East Coast Under Date 31st of July 1741/ lodge, [and] the Tumenggung Datta Gueda Mangoenagara and Djaja Poeder ga, but that they held [position] before the fortress and let [it be] requested that the commandant van Velse would come outside to receive that money, as happened, when the said Tumenggung Djaja Soederga dealt the commandant such a treacherous blow that he died from it immediately. That the lodge was thereupon immediately closed, and by the Company [soldiers] being in it, European servants with the cannon fired upon the said Tumenggung and the Javanese with him, when the Tumenggung Mangaenagara and Djaja Soederga fell, along with some lesser [men]. Item [also] the Tumenggung Natta Juda was severely wounded. After which event the commanding lieutenant Nicolaas Wiltvang from the Kraton [palace] betook himself within the fortress. After which done From Java's East Coast under Date 31st of July 1747. report the Javanese Marta Troena remained silent. text_translated_detailed: posts after half past seven o'clock, namely first at the post located beside the palisade of Sergeant Balthazax Ero, where he held the watch, then at one likewise behind the palisade of the Mardijker Koridon Anthonij where sailors keep watch, also then the sergeants of the west and east barriers of the aforementioned must be given notice, to be on guard and keep good watch, not only on the Chinese, but further on all those who wished to commit hostilities. Also, with the clock striking seven o'clock, to have the barriers closed in like manner: all of the same has been carried out. Subsequently, annexed to this is a letter by Your Excellency's esteemed hand, per the returned messengers of that Madura Pangerang Adepattij Tsjacraniagrat to the Under-Merchant and Resident Zacharias De Bensin at Rembang, which has now been brought back here for the second time by the Javanese Jiwo Mangalo and Tsitra Joeda; who declare that they, due to the insecurity of the Chinese surrounding that place, have not dared or been able to approach the aforementioned fortress, being afraid that they would be discovered as bearers of a secret message, which is to be communicated to Your Excellency's esteemed person, that on the 15th of this month, the Yacht Anthonia appeared here at the roadstead from Batavia with such cash and goods as Their High Excellencies have been pleased to allocate for one year for the benefit of this eastern corner, as appears from the annexed copy of the bills of lading and invoice, together with the copy of the aforementioned Their High and Most Esteemed Excellencies' always honored letter of the 21st of this month. We express our humble gratitude for this, and we shall have that vessel return as soon as possible, with as much rice as it can carry away and place in the meantime. From Java, South Coast, dated 31st July 1741. /

It appears that His Honor is now extremely embittered against the Javanese as ever before, because he cannot hear the slightest thing. [undersigned] Agrees [signed] P.L. Barenclouw, Secretary's Copy. We have taken up that work on the 12th of this month, and with the assistance of the pangerang-adepattij [regional administrator] Tjacraningrat, to Madura, together with the Surabayan and Gresik Javanese, we have already destroyed a good portion of that harmful rabble, such that Your Excellencies are ordered to ensure that the small vessel here remains loaded, so that the pangerang's subordinates, the Company's subjects from Sumanap and Pamacassan, of whom a good number are expected here daily to protect us, as well as Javanese and all other merchants who do not appear to wish to commit hostilities against us, shall not be molested by Your Excellencies' sailors, but rather treated in a friendly manner. text_translated_detailed: [signed:] P[ieter] L[ucas] BaerenClouw: secretary Surabaya. Benjamin Blom, To the Merchant of Java's east coast 31st of July 1741, chief together with the council. Your Excellencies' writings of the 23rd instant we have received with the papers mentioned therein, whose contents have been accepted for communication, finding it equally necessary to note hereby that it has been approved to endorse Your Excellencies' disposition made regarding the distribution of the Chinese vessels found at cost after the massacre of that nation under the murmuring garrison, just as Your Excellencies are to be qualified to act in similar fashion with the remaining Chinese houses. Meanwhile, it is noteworthy that the chief regent of Sumanap, the Radeen Tommongong Tjacranagara, has been newly instructed to assist Surabaya and Pasuruan first, whose original Javanese missive together with one to the Madurese pangerang ade pattij Tjacraningrat of Java's east coast under Date 31st of July 1741 follow hereupon, which must receive a secure arrangement in loco as soon as possible, while the annexed Dutch copies thereof shall provide a complete elucidation, just as the relevant Extract from Their High Excellencies' missive to us of the 30th of the last week of the month, and copy of open commission, from which it shall appear that the first signed has assumed authority from Commander Bartholomeus Visscher and is here publicly presented to the people as chief merchant and governor of this coast, after which the same presentation shall also have to take place at cost according to custom. Meanwhile, we communicate that we are still not in a position to be able to satisfy Your Excellencies' petition for European military and seafaring personnel, as well as inland vessels; however, we shall of Java's east coast under Date 31st of July 1741 first arrange the necessary small vessels for the removal of the rice stored there and missing — with which, under friendly greetings, we remain [understood:] Your Excellencies' good friends [was signed] Abraham Roos, h[eer] Coorenaar Const[antijn] Sibens, J[ohn] Meijerhoff f[rom] M[ister]'s v[an] d[er] Huijden, P[eter] de Vos, J[ohn]'s Tonneman Junior, and R[udolf] de Klerk, [in margin:] Samarang the 28th of July in the year 1741. [understood:] Agrees. [signed:] I[saac]'s L[ucas] BaerenClouw: secretary. Resolution and Council taken on the 20th of July in the year 1741. All Present. text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast under Date 31st of July 1741, Samarang, the 6th of July, Anno 1741. [below] P. S. By this we make known that Their High Excellencies have been pleased to honor the Governor Visscher with the quality and salary of Commandeur [Commander], which Your Excellency shall have to use in the writing of letters as well as otherwise for information. [below] Agrees [signed] P. L. Baerenclouw, secretary.—Samarang. To the Honourable and Esteemed Mister Bartholomeus Visscher, Commandeur on and along Java's northeast Coast, together with the Council there. Title. This serves as an escort for two enclosed Javanese letters, to the messenger Dain Managala, and his brother the fellow Macassar Dain Ingabeij, and since their content is of importance [for] From Java's East Coast under date 31st of July 1741, so far as we can understand, we judge, and therefore send them to Your Honour with all speed, the more so since we have certain news that a great number of Chinese and Javanese are standing about an hour from here, and also already a great plot from Samarang is on its way hither. With which we break off in haste, and with all respect remain [below] Title [lower] Your Honour's most humble Servants [was signed] Lambert Lepeltak and R. Engelink [in margin] Japara, the 19th of July, Anno 1741. P. S. The conduct of the aforementioned Dain Managala has seemed to us rather suspicious beforehand, therefore we shall henceforth watch carefully over his conduct, as he is very closely related to Aria Coedoes and other chiefs of the Japara people. [below] Agrees [signed] P. L. Baerenclouw, secretary. Samarang. To the Honourable and Esteemed Mister Bartholomeus Visscher, From Java's East Coast under Date 31st of July 1741. Commandeur on and along Java's northeast Coast, together with the Council. Title. In fulfillment of the old friendship which existed between my father and Your Excellency, I make Your Excellency mindful not to [engage] in the From Java's East Coast under Date 31st of July 1741 war which is being waged by the aforementioned Jopanese Chinese, for if Your Excellency will conduct yourself thus, I shall stand by the Company or Your Excellency against me in war, but on the contrary, if Your Excellency will take the good of the Macassars and Buginese to heart, follow me, or else my brother the Adepatty [uncertain: Adepatty] Jutaasoema, for I know how to say that to you if you truly recognize me as your friend. In the peace of Java, love me, trust in me, and fear not that the Chinese will molest you. Be pleased to let me know whether Your Excellency will fulfill this or not. [below] Translated by me [signed] I. Lesueur [below] Agrees [signed] P. L. Baerenclouw, secretary. Samarang. text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast, dated 31st July 1741. Regarding the war that is being waged by the aforementioned Chinese, if you, Your Excellency, wage war, I shall stand with the Company or with you against me. But on the contrary, if you, Your Excellency, take the good of the Makassarese and Buginese to heart, follow me, or rather my brother the Adepatty Jutaasoema, for I am able to tell you of this. If you, Your Excellency, truly acknowledge me as your friend and love the peace of Java, trust in me and do not fear that the Chinese will molest you. Please let me know whether you, Your Excellency, will comply with this or not. [Understood.] Translated by me. [Signed.] I.S. Agrees. [Signed.] P. L. Baeren Clouw, Secretary. [Understood.] Samarang. To the Esteemed and Honorable Mister Bartholomeus Visscher, Commander on and along Java's North Coast. From Java's East Coast, dated 31st July 1741. Together with the Council. Title. [I] hereby inform your Esteemed Excellency that here on the 17th [of this month] the ship has arrived here at the roadstead of Rembang, and has approached me with the small boat so near to the aforementioned anchorage that the same can assist in many ways with the cannon and has not failed to continue therein with all vigilance. But I must inform your Esteemed Excellency with sorrow that the discontented Chinese have so completely surrounded the Company's anchorage that the Esteemed Mister Resident Benzin has been forced to retire therein with the Company's servants and to close and defend the gate with all his strength. But due to the guard being kept by this wretched rabble, no one can come out or go in. Therefore, until now the Company has not been able to deliver the goods received. From Java's East Coast, dated 31st July 1741, which brings the same into great distress regarding the means of life. The means and ammunition of war through daily consumption are very much seen to be consumed, and I am not in a position, being weak, to deliver the same by hand if it cannot be taken from the shore, for with my small force I cannot undertake such a thing, while according to rumor there are well over two thousand armed men who do not let the anchorage rest day and night, just as happened again last night with shooting from their cannon and setting fires, in order to set the anchorage ablaze with everything, which the Almighty shall prevent. Today the bailiff Intje Amatt of Costij came aboard me with the Company's letter from your Esteemed Excellency for the Esteemed Mister Resident Benzin in a small canoe, and delivered to me the message that he has been hidden here for 12 days already. From Java's East Coast, dated 31st July 1741, and could find no opportunity to deliver the same. In your Esteemed Excellency's good pleasure, I take the liberty to inform you that if no more military reinforcements come for the Company, it will run into great danger and will have to resort to an irregular and presumptuous course. With this, your Esteemed Excellency, I come in all humility to request to be provided for the unavoidable service of 2000 pounds of gunpowder, 800 pieces of round shot of 4 pounds, 200 pieces of the same of 2 pounds, 6 pieces of linen for making cartridges, 1.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast, dated 31st July 1741. Report Given to the Esteemed and Honorable Mister Bartholomeus Visscher, Commander on and along Java's North Coast, by the discreet quartermaster Hendrik Schrittels of the Company's straw-pantjallang De Haaij. A relator says that it is now several days ago that he received orders from the head of this well-esteemed Esteemed and Honorable Mister Commander to sail from this roadstead and set course toward Rembang in order to inquire how matters stood there, and likewise to learn from the under-merchant and resident Zacharias Debenzin whether the relator's small boat could be of any service at that place, or to proceed further from there toward Surabaya in conformity with which order the relator. From Java's East Coast, dated 31st July 1741, set the stern toward that direction and on the 17th of this month arrived at the roadstead of the aforementioned residence in 2 fathoms of water, letting the anchor fall approximately half an hour. After that, there came sailing toward him, the relator, 4 strong prau-maiyangs, being together completely covered with buffalo hides and strongly mounted with cannons. Also an uncountable number of Chinese and among them also some Javanese, all dressed in red with high caps on their heads of the said color. For this reason, the relator, seeing the approaching misfortune and being afraid, resolved for the preservation of their lives and the Company's small boat to cut the anchor rope and to run before the wind between the islands back here, being constantly pursued by the aforementioned prau-maiyangs and being called upon by the Chinese that the relator should furl the sail. But seeing that. From Java's East Coast, dated 31st July 1741, this was not complied with, they fired sharp shot at the small pantjallang, and which the relator did not leave unanswered, so

Resolution taken in Council on the 21st July in the year 1741. All present. — From Java's east coast under date 31 July 1741. The bookkeeper Simon Pierre Salie, having appeared on the ship Nieuwland, made known that the ship's authorities, according to received ordinance, had handed over to the Ambonese free burgher Fredrik Willem the vessel Koning with its seafaring crew and goods that had come from Makassar under the command of the Juragan Pietenko belonging to the one nominated as sailor Be Tjamko on the pass document, with the acknowledgment that the common people on the ships were very murmuring about this and that the boatswains and other minor officers were present in order to request the council to speak with them, to which they were permitted by the ship's authorities, for the reason that they had not wished to place credence in the instruction given here and presented to them, thus it was allowed to let their people come in order to somewhat calm and reassure them, being from Java's east coast under date 31 July 1741. text_translated_detailed: Year 1741. From Java's South Coast, dated the 6th of August 1741, received. [Underlined:] Most Esteemed, Highly Respected, and Greatly Honored Sir and Well-Esteemed Gentlemen. [Below:] Your Most Esteemed, Highly Respected, and Greatly Honored, most obedient and loyally obligated Servant, [signed:] L.S. Grothe, [in margin:] Tagal, the 6th of August, 1741. Batavia. To His Excellency the Most Esteemed, Highly Respected, and Greatly Honored Sir Adriaan Valckenier, Governor-General, and the Well-Esteemed Gentlemen Councillors of the Netherlands Indies; — received the 10th of August. Most Esteemed, Highly Respected, and Greatly Honored, Earnest, Courageous, Wise, Prudent, and Most Generous Sir and Well-Esteemed Gentlemen. It was on the 4th of this month that the undersigned arrived here with the ships Beekvliet and West-Cappel. Your Most Esteemed, Highly Respected, and Greatly Honored, having received the missive from Java's South Coast dated the 6th of August 1741 from the resident Grothe, I presented to the aforementioned resident the orders from Your Most Esteemed, Highly Respected, and Greatly Honored, that three hundred native laborers would remain here for the protection of the rice harvest. Upon this, I had the Macassar Captain Daing Mabella come ashore with his people. However, since the long-awaited sixteen hundred native soldiers from Cheribon have arrived here, upon whose arrival not only all Chinese but also the Javanese have withdrawn, I believe the aforementioned sixteen hundred natives will be sufficiently capable of resisting any hostile force here. Therefore, I have had Captain Daing Mabella and his people return to the ship in order, God willing, to set sail this evening toward Semarang. I also have the honor to respectfully notify Your Most Esteemed, Highly Respected, and Greatly Honored of Java's South Coast, dated the 6th of August 1741, that the freeman from Semarang, Nicolaas Zachariasz, having arrived here with seventy-five bales in a solitary state, having lost his rudder, anchor rope, and sail, I have, in hope of Your Most Esteemed, Highly Respected, and Greatly Honored's approval, divided the aforementioned seventy-five bales between the two ships

When these are defeated by the enemies, but when one attacks our forces and the Company retreats and does not dare to advance, and that the Company gives all peoples a bad name, which greatly troubles a noble heart. Indeed, even Poerbaija has been banished, who had committed not the slightest wrong. Therefore, I respect and must ensure that no child's child of the same from Java's South Coast, dated the 6th of August 1741, shall ever show any good to the Company's servants. All this was spoken at the ordinary gathering place in the presence of all mantries and princes. Upon which the Raden Diepattij and Raden Pringalaija, together with all the further princes there, answered the Emperor: it is truly true that the Company takes power on the Island of Java, just as the Emperor of Rome does. All these aforementioned matters the Raden Tommagom of Siedaijoe has made known to the Captain and Lieutenant at Cartasura, although the aforementioned Captain and Lieutenant have paid little attention to the counsel of the aforementioned Pangerang.

All these aforementioned matters the Raden Tommagom of Siedaijoe has made known to the Captain and Lieutenant at Cartasura, although the aforementioned Captain and Lieutenant have paid little attention to the counsel of the aforementioned Pangerang. I make all this known so that the Company may come to know the talk of all the regents who are on Java. Also, their intention is to join with the rebellious Chinese of Semarang to destroy the lodge there, and that of Tjankals or so westward, and when Semarang shall be brought under from Java's South Coast, dated the 6th of August 1741, their intention is also to destroy Cheribon, and when the Chinese have overcome Rambang, they will join themselves with Raden Pringalaija and march toward Surabaja to likewise destroy the aforementioned place. Our most recent humble letter to your High Excellency and Great Respectability was sent under date of the 31st of the past month by the Panjallang the Seagull, to which we humbly refer in this regard, sent solely under the escort of Captain Rudolph Carel von Glan, the Lieutenant Gerrit Hendrik Alepkelt, the bookkeeper Anthonij Arnout and assistant Jan Gustaaf Carel van Glan, sons of the aforementioned Captain, whom we have permitted under the favorable approval of your High Excellency and Great Respectability to follow their father, whose closed salary accounts are enclosed herewith, and who have all been embarked according to request on the Chialoup [small boat] of that inland burgher Constantijn Plache, with which we express our due and deep respect. text_translated_detailed: Received 27th August, year 1741. From Java's South Coast, 14th August 1741. No. 17: Four letters from Japara and two likewise in answer. Samarang, 19th August, Year 1741. To his Excellency the High Noble Gentlemen Adriaan Valckenier, Governor General and the Noble Gentlemen Councillors of the Netherlands Indies: — High Noble, Stern, Great esteemed, Earnest, Valiant, Wise, Provident, Most Generous, Widely commanding Lord and well Noble Gentlemen. Ed„le Agtbaeren Heer en Heeren Gerard van Krombruggen schipper op het te desen rheede leggende schip Proostwijk, uw Ed:e agtbare onderdanige dienaer versoekt seer nedrig omme met de nodige verversingen randsoen voor de reijse nae Batavia tot behoef der scheepelingen door de goedheijd van uw Ed:e agtbare te mogen werden voorsien. 7 zoo is met Eenparige stemmen dat versoek billijk g'oordeelt beslooten daarinne te condescendeeren en hier van Eerbiedig kennis te geven aan haar hoog Edelheedens met nedrige imploratie dat volgens wissel brief aan het Eerwaarde collegie van boedelmeesteren ter gedagte Jndias hoofd plaats mag werden voldaan zodanigen somma van Van Javas O:t Cust onder Dato 14:' aug:s 1741. text_translated_detailed: from Java's East Coast, dated the 14th of August 1741, chief merchant and governor of Java's Northeast Coast together with the Council. Honorable Esteemed Lord and Gentlemen, Gerard van Krombruggen, skipper of the ship Proost Wijk lying here at this roadstead, your Honorable Esteemed humble servant requests most humbly to be provided with the necessary refreshments and rations for the voyage to Batavia for the benefit of the ship's crew through the kindness of your Honorable Esteemed. Thus it is with unanimous votes that the request is justly deemed and resolved to accede therein and to give respectful notice thereof to their High Excellencies with humble supplication that according to bill of exchange to the Honorable college of estate masters at the aforesaid Indies' chief place such a sum may be paid, from Java's East Coast under date the 14th of August 1741, of nine thousand six hundred eighty-seven rixdollars [modern equivalent: Dutch East India Company currency] and five stuivers [modern equivalent: small Dutch coin] at 48 silver stuivers per rixdollar, which according to shown accounts after deduction of ordinary expenses for the benefit of the estate of the fugitive Chinese named Konks and for the account of the apprehended former captain of the Chinese nation at Batavia Nie Hoekong have been resting under the secretary Pieter Leonard Barenclouw, likewise by him paid into the Company's cash there, Semarang in Council dated aforesaid, /:was signed:/ and Roos, H. Title: From Java's East Coast, dated August 14th, 1741. With Sergeant Pieter van Keekelen and six native soldiers, we had on the 23rd of this month the honor of dispatching our last humble letter to Your Esteemed Excellency, to which we have humbly attended, and since then we were on the 28th thereof honored by dispatch to Pasuruan, the home of sailor Dirk van Heinsberg, with Your Esteemed Excellency's missive of the 20th previous, wherein Your Esteemed Excellency graciously permits us, both for this garrison and for the Sumatran and Makassarese peoples who have already appeared here, to the number of 1500 heads under the Sumatran Sourabadiningat Raden and Raden Mancoenagora of Makassar, to qualify ourselves for the purchase of rice (as much as shall be possible and can be stored, which would be the first obligation to be fulfilled in case the native did not mostly altogether depart thus toward Djipan, where Raden Soerangrana is stationed, as elsewhere, and likewise the grain, here therefore left uncut in the field and bringing almost nothing more to market; yet we shall do our best to gather as much as shall be possible to happen, while we your Excellency

Item, that the Prince had the Lord Commandant van Velse called to court several times, but that the latter always refused, for the reason that he would have heard that Pangerang Martasana, Raden Djaja Koessoema, together with the seventh deposed Tommongong Soespanagara of Batang, had made it known that the Emperor wished to act falsely against the Company, which having come to the Prince's ears, he had them put to death, so that the Lord Commandant thereby gaining a better opinion of his Majesty, with the commanding Lieutenant Wiltvang went to the court to wait upon the Prince. text_translated_detailed: Benjamin Blom, To the Merchants departing and Vincent van Wingerden, arriving, chief together with the council. Whereas their High Excellencies have resolved by missive of the 22nd of the last passed month, as appears from the attached Extract, graciously to agree to the request made by the merchant Blom to be released to the Netherlands, and that as his replacement from Java's East Coast under date 14th August 1741, the second merchant Vincent van Wingerden has been chosen, who now travels by the sloop Gosowina, for which reason the aforementioned must make a proper transfer of the said fortress and the Company's effects to the latter in such a manner that the same come to be sorted under his responsibility, and then, together with the delivery of a memorandum for the information of his equally replaced predecessor, he may depart. In the meantime, we have been able to discern from various of your letters that suspicion is being harbored regarding the conduct of the Madurese Pangeran Adipati Tsjacraningrat, as if he were not living in good harmony with the Company. In order to dispel such thoughts, we send herewith a copy of a letter from the aforementioned prince directed to their High Excellencies with the answer thereto, whose content may serve for your information, while we within a few days your Excellency's made from Java's East Coast under date 14th August 1741: request for peoples and war ammunition, both for Surabaya and Pasuruan, shall be competent according to necessity, with which under friendly greetings we remain Your Excellency's good friends [was signed:] A.m Roos, H.k Korenaar, Const.n Siebens, J.n Meijer Hoff, s.n M: v: d: Heijden, P.r de Vos, J.s Tonneman Junior, and R.r de Klerk, [in margin:] Semarang, 11th August, year 1741. text_translated_detailed:
From Java's South Coast, dated 14th August 1741: A petition for troops and military ammunition, as much for Surabaya as for Pasuruan, shall be provided according to necessity, with which we remain your good friends. [Was signed:] A.M. Roos, H. Korenaar, Const. Sibens, J.N. Meijerhoff, S.N. M. v.d. Heijden, P.R. Devos, J.S. Tonneman Junior, and R.R. de Klerk. [In margin:] Semarang, 11th August, year 1741. [Undersigned:] Agrees, Baeren Clouw, Secretary. [Signed:] J.

To His Excellency the High and Noble Lord Adriaan Valckenier, Governor General, and the Noble Lords Councillors of the Netherlands Indies; High and Noble, strict and far-ruling Lord, and well-born Noble Lords.

Noachobree, of Amsterdam, your High and Noble greatly esteemed and entirely submissive [servant]. All of which [is] from Java's South Coast, dated 14th August 1741, and obedient servant since the year 1717, per the ship the Hopvogel [Hopbird], arrived here as a soldier for 9 guilders [ƒ9], and since then in the year 1733, through the gracious favor of your High Excellencies, promoted to ensign, in which capacity at this office of Surabaya is serving militarily. Now takes the liberty, in order that upon the arrival of reinforcements for this garrison your High Excellencies may be implored, so that through that same dear benevolence may be benefited with the rank of lieutenant, which singular favor shall always be merited through vigilance in service. [Undersigned:] Which doing, etc.

To His Excellency the High and Noble Lord Adriaan Valckenier, Governor General, and the Noble Lords Councillors of the Netherlands Indies, as here before. From Java's South Coast, dated 14th August.

High and Noble, strict and far-ruling Lord, and well-born Noble Lords.

Ambrosius Klein van Valkenburg, near Maastricht, your High and Noble greatly esteemed and entirely submissive and obedient servant, since the year 1726, per the ship Wickenburg, arrived here as a soldier for 9 guilders [ƒ9], and subsequently in the preceding year successively advanced to sergeant, with twenty guilders per month, and for which at this office of Surabaya has been assigned, now takes the liberty your High Excellencies to implore, in order that upon the promotion of the ensign High Obree as lieutenant, so that through their benevolence his place as ensign may be succeeded to, which singular favor shall always be merited through vigilance in the service. [Undersigned:] Which doing, etc. Translation Javanese.

From Java's South Coast, dated 14th August 1741.

Missive sent by the Pangerang Adipati Tjacraningrat from Madura to the Noble and esteemed Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, commander on and along the northeast coast to Semarang, received on the 1st August 1741.

After customary preamble, I make known to your Excellency that the Raden Tumenggung Soeradiningrat has arrived at Sadajoe, leaving Salatiga without informing the other regents there of the matter, for the reason that at the said place an order came from the Susuhunan that the Javanese ministers should proceed from there via Jipang to Surabaya in order to attack that office, just as has happened before the prince at Kartasura, where the Captain, Lieutenant, and all Company servants who held the canton post have fallen, though the lodge has remained standing. Of the Emperor's subjects, the Ingabei Samarandana died there and the Rijxbestierder [Regional Administrator] and Tumenggung Natta Joeda and Sirta Wigoena were wounded. Regarding the regents of Surabaya, they are positioned at the village of Padangan, located in the land of Jipang, having orders to wrest Surabaya, Gresik, and Lamongan from my hands and bring them back to the Emperor. These regents were met by order of the Surabaya chief with 2,000 of my subjects commanded by the Ingabei Wiera Patti, Raden Dipanagara, and Raden Waseeng Sarie, who gave battle to the aforementioned regents on Jipang and put them to flight, without having heard anything further. The Surabaya inhabitants hold themselves still in balance, not being able to say whether they follow the prince or me, though I do not believe they would willingly be submissive to me.

To the Pangerang Adipati Tjacradiningrat at Madura.

Your Excellency, my brother, the envoys recently sent back by you, I have had the honor to write to your Excellency, and thereupon by order of their High Excellencies an act of discharge from the Susuhunan's slavery under the protection of the Company has been granted. Subsequently I have received with much eagerness your very pleasant missive, containing principally the happy arrival of your beloved son the Raden and Tumenggung Soeradiningrat, which has greatly rejoiced my heart, although the further news in the same letter would have been able to sadden it, in that by orders of the Susuhunan the Kartasura garrison was placed in peril, the commandant and lieutenant of the canton with its garrison fell, and that your brother's brave subjects were also sought by his Majesty. But what shall I say of it, except that the good inclination of the prince has become corrupted through the faction of Surabaya, which your brother has not been able to tolerate for so many years, much less the treatment of the previous ministers, since they have used their sovereign as a wax figure in order to seek their interests from it, and relatives who are like snakes to be made great, which ones have now brought the Javanese Kingdom into a corrupted state.

I make known to Your Excellency that Your Excellency's younger brother from Java, South Coast, under Date 14th August 1741, the tommongong of Sidayu has absconded with the flight from Salatiga to his former territory, having withdrawn because the Susuhunan and the other regents present there ordered him to attack the fortress of Surabaya in a hostile manner, just as the Cartasoerase settlements had been overcome by him, having caused the captain and lieutenant to be killed. However, the lodge has defended itself until now. text_translated_detailed: To the sub-merchant Laurens Grothe, Resident there; — Esteemed, pious, and discreet [person], Your Excellency: We have received your letter dated the 3rd of this month, together with the attachments belonging thereto, to which in response it should be noted that Your Excellency was qualified to hold 1600 native coolies [workers] that arrived at Tagal for the strengthening of the post with 600 soldiers. Furthermore, Your Excellency shall arrange for the remaining [coolies] to be sent here as soon as possible. However, when the aforementioned number of 600 men is no longer required for the cost, we shall also meet them from Java's south coast under the date of the 14th of August in the year 1741, since our office is besieged all around by enemies and has need of them. In the meantime, we shall upon the arrival of the ship Meijenberg provide Your Excellency with a vessel in order to store the Company's cash therein, and likewise to provision it with such products as shall be found with Your Excellency and shall be required for Batavia, and we hope that since the enemies have been defeated, it shall be possible to become master of the rice harvest and thus also to satisfy our made demand for said grain. We have found it good to approve the testamentary disposition of the sergeant Henning Beuk; therefore the aforementioned instrument shall be returned here to the interested parties, while we shall await the like documents in original from Java's south coast under the date of the 14th of August 1741 in copy. text_translated_clean: To the sub-merchant Laurens Grothe, Resident there; — Esteemed, pious, and discreet person, Your Excellency: We have received your letter dated the 3rd of this month, together with the attachments belonging thereto, to which in response it should be noted that Your Excellency was qualified to hold 1600 native coolies workers that arrived at Tagal for the strengthening of the post with 600 soldiers. Furthermore, Your Excellency shall arrange for the remaining coolies to be sent here as soon as possible. However, when the aforementioned number of 600 men is no longer required for the cost, we shall also meet them from Java's south coast under the date of the 14th of August in the year 1741, since our office is besieged all around by enemies and has need of them. In the meantime, we shall upon the arrival of the ship Meijenberg provide Your Excellency with a vessel in order to store the Company's cash therein, and likewise to provision it with such products as shall be found with Your Excellency and shall be required for Batavia, and we hope that since the enemies have been defeated, it shall be possible to become master of the rice harvest and thus also to satisfy our made demand for said grain. We have found it good to approve the testamentary disposition of the sergeant Henning Beuk; therefore the aforementioned instrument shall be returned here to the interested parties, while we shall await the like documents in original from Java's south coast under the date of the 14th of August 1741 in copy. Samarang, To the Honourable and Esteemed Mister Abraham Roos, chief merchant and governor, on a post along Java's east coast together with the Council. Title Your Honour's esteemed and valued letters of the 27th of the last month that has passed, have been well received by us, from which we have understood the fortunate arrival of the Noble and esteemed Mister Abraham Roos as chief merchant and governor of this coast, and that his Honour as such was presented there with orders to us to likewise have this done here according to custom and under the reading of the open commission by their High Excellencies the high government of Dutch India to the aforementioned mister governor delivered, and in copy together with an Extract from their High Excellencies of Java's east coast under Date 14th August 1741, great and esteemed missive, sent to us; so we have, their esteemed contents, on the first of this month in the presence of the Macassan and Malay chiefs together with all the Company's servants presented the Noble and esteemed Mister Abraham Roos, as our governor and commander, to the people who unanimously and we in particular have had the honour to congratulate his Honour on that high and important office, praying that the Almighty may direct and bless his counsel, decisions and undertakings for the welfare of the Netherlands East India Company and the lustre of his Honour. In the meantime the first undersigned most humbly requests of your Honour to be willing to express his humble gratitude to the aforementioned their High Excellencies at an opportune moment through favourable appointment as captain, further in response to your Honour's esteemed letters of the 2nd of this month

text_translated_detailed: /:was signed/ L: Baeren Clouw secretary of Java's east coast under Date 14th August 1741 Samarang; To the Honourable and Esteemed Mister Abraham Roos, chief merchant, and Governor on a post along Java's north and east coast together with the Council. Title: your Honour's esteemed letters of the 6th of this month having been well delivered to us, so it is respectfully answered that we have placed ourselves as much as possible in a state of defence against all hostile attacks, but as regards the means of subsistence, these are now no longer to be obtained, because the enemy approaches day by day, and has already dared to undertake two attacks on the Macassan and Malay outposts, which were by the aforementioned natives the first time bravely and courageously driven back, and now yesterday a much greater force of rebels approaching on the Posser road, our men /:having suffered one dead and one wounded/ in good order while firing withdrew from Java's east coast under Date 14th August 1741, whereupon we from the lodge with the heavy cannon fired so well that the enemies in all haste took flight, scarcely giving themselves time to carry away their dead and wounded. In the meantime we take the liberty to insert again the request of the Macassan and Malay ensign-bearers with respect to their advancement to lieutenant in our respectful writing done on the 4th of May, as they have already served 37 years in that capacity, and this would serve as further encouragement, with which we wish that the ships from Batavia will soon come into view so that if we still need some cannonballs, red balls, scrap, etc., together with muskets, cartridge pouches, flints and cartridge paper as well as payment for garrison costs, to be sold to the European and native garrison to obtain breaking off, and with respectful Java's east coast under Date 14th August 1741, greeting with all reverence and respect

text_translated_detailed: Jos Tonneman, Junior and R., the clerk, [in margin:] Semarang, the 2nd of August in the year 1741. P.S. The ensign Jan Fredriksz, mentioned in our most recent letters of the 27th of July last past, shall remain here for so long as Java's East Coast [Javasat Cust] under Date the 14th of August 1741, until the recruits expected from Batavia arrive, when Captain Engelink shall be replaced by the same [person, understood] the replacement P. Baeren. Agreed, [signed] L. Rouw, secretary. Japara. To the under-merchant Lambertz Lepeltack, Resident, together with the Council. Esteemed, pious, discreet [persons]; Your letter of yesterday's date having been received here, it serves in answer that we do not doubt that you will be placed in a position by this office to be able to assist with the necessary provisions, since one sees that the Company's rightful weapons have scattered the five others. In the meantime, we have seen fit for the encouragement of service, on approbation, to appoint from His High Excellency's [approval] to Java's East Coast [Javasat Cust] under Date the 14th of August 1741, lieutenants who serve militarily at the coast, namely Dain Managal and Jntje Alie of the Malay and Makassarese nations, while the ensign Jan Fredriksz now travels by the Pantjallang, the East-Ender, in which are also embarked 30 inland soldiers with their non-commissioned officers for the strengthening of your garrison. Furthermore, there lie beside two bills of lading and invoices of the cash and war ammunition which you receive by the bearer of this, and Captain Engelink shall have to remain there until further orders in order to act as head of the militia; with which, under friendly greetings, we remain [understood] your good friend [was signed:] A. text_translated_detailed: Regarding the transport of supplies over Grobogan, it is further reported that the garrison at Cartasoera, numbering 190 men, due to lack of provisions, raised a white flag and opened the gates of the fortress, whereupon they would have received pardon from the Emperor. However, they were all placed in chains and must serve under the Chinese in order to march forward for the use of the cannon, etc. But since the aforementioned reports concerning this last point are very uncertain, the Governor and Council of Java, under date of 25 August 1741, considers the narrated account merely as proper communication, while we have no doubt that the Susuhunang's company has been assisted by the enemy with cannons, all the more so since those noted here are marked with Javanese letters, and such heavy artillery is not to be found on Java as at Cartasoera. In the continuation of this matter regarding the situation here, we have the honor to advise that after previous deliberation in the war council on the 15th and 20th of this month, it was resolved to attack the enemy, which was effectuated on the day following, when the Almighty, after the fierce and desperate fire of the Company's weapons, blessed our arms with victory, whereby we have become master of the Chinese kampong [village] and some of their outer works, extending toward the Dalm of the party Djajadi, from Java, South Coast, under date of 25 August 1741, the house of the former lieutenant que jonko, to the southern road, which positions are now occupied in order to be able to withstand all attacks, under which attack the Company's officers and militia conducted themselves with particular bravery, having captured from the enemy 44 pieces of cannon of various sorts and 4 flags, and of our people in total 50 dead and 109 wounded in the broad [sense], a copy of the report to be seen in the form of the day register drawn up and signed.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's south coast under date of the 25th of August 1741, in the year 1741. It is hereby agreed, gotten. Haeren Clouw, secretary. P. Resolution taken on the 1st of August 179 in the Council of Policy; All. The council being seated, it was proposed by the mister governor Roos that since this establishment is now so well supported by their High Excellencies with military forces that it is placed in a position to be able to attack the establishment's enemies, and moreover the necessary war ammunition being provided, whether it was not necessary to establish a war council in order that through their deliberation the necessary measures be taken, and inasmuch as this was unanimously deemed by the council to be most necessary, it is therefore decided to put the same into effect immediately and that the aforementioned council shall consist of 3 captains of this garrison. From Java's south coast under date of the 25th of August 1741. 6 lieutenants and all captains of. Furthermore, in consideration having taken into account that the aforementioned native council must have its own secretary, in order that the affairs may be expedited all the more speedily, it is therefore deemed best to appoint the bookkeeper and first sworn clerk here, Jacob De Haas, to that position with the quality of sub-merchant, and to have the assistant Jan Biler serve in his place, though all subject to the approval of their High Excellencies, in which manner also promoted is the lieutenant of the free Balinese nation here, Batjoe, on account of his brave conduct, to captain, and the here-stationed constable Hendrik Smit Janson of Rotterdam, on account of shown vigilance in service, to ensign of the aforementioned militia. text_translated_detailed: A report of an ensign or sergeant with eight to ten common soldiers, principally to encourage the troops from Java's south coast under date 2nd August 1741, yet if so many Europeans cannot be spared, that the Sumatran peoples might be provided with them instead; further making it known in plain terms that otherwise with the slightest advantage for the Company, nothing can be undertaken because the enemy is already too powerful, and through the conquest of Rembang is growing considerably. Gentlemen van Loo and Hartting reported to me further that the Pangerang was in no way inclined to let himself be drawn out anywhere, although it seemed extraordinary, and the Prince also appeared to be in good humor with one of his attendants, having let it be known to the aforementioned ensign that the Raden Soerangana and the Tumenggung of Djipan in that district have been defeated by his subordinates with a loss of approximately 200 dead by estimation, besides the wounded, among whom was a son of the aforementioned Tumenggung, but otherwise no one of note from Java's south coast under date 25th August 1741. Meanwhile, we have received through an extract from Her High Excellencies' missive to Your Honour of the 30th of June of this year, and a copy of the open commission, that Your Honour has assumed authority from His Honour the Commandeur Bartholomeus Visscher, and has already been presented to the people publicly at the head comptoir Samarang as chief merchant and governor of this coast, which here on the 3rd of the same month was likewise carried out in the honorable manner with the required ceremonies, and notice thereof was given to Madura, Sumanap, and Pamacassan so that it might likewise be effectuated there according to custom. While we have the honor to congratulate Your Honour most reverently as our superior, with the wish for a fortunate governance concerning Your Honour.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast under Date 25th August 1748 Semarang. To the Esteemed and Honorable Sir Abraham Roos, chief merchant and commander on and along Java's North East Coast together with the Council. Title. — Your Esteemed and Honorable and learned letters of the date of the 2nd of this month have been most dutifully brought to us, together with the cash and war ammunition according to the invoice, for the provision of which we offer our humble thanks, just as the arrangements made in Makassar and with Alie of the Makassarese in Malay fashion are also being made for their appointment as lieutenants, while we further make known that the 30 native soldiers with their non-commissioned officers for the strengthening of this garrison for the performance of service have been properly placed from Java's East Coast under Date 2nd August 1741, requesting that at an opportunity we may obtain a name roll of the same. Since your esteemed letter has arrived here at the roadstead, the ship Christina Sophia, which vessel we humbly request to be allowed to keep here, as it can cause much damage to the enemy, as has been evident on the 12th of this month when the rebels undertook to erect a fortification of coconut trees on the seacoast, but by your efforts through the cannonading from the aforementioned ship as well as from the shallop of the bearer of this letter, the Makassarese burgher Matthijs Tourien, some measures have been prevented. For the rest, having nothing further to write, this letter should accompany the requested specification of cannonballs and other sharp ammunition of various kinds, flints, etc., remaining with deep respect from Java's East Coast under date 25th August 1741 and with respect. text_translated_detailed: Java East Coast dated 25 August 1741. Resolution taken in war council at the head office Semarang on Tuesday the 15th August 1741 in the morning at half past seven o'clock, all present: The chief merchant and commander of this Coast Abraham Roos; Bergopman [mountain commander] Nathanaal Steinmets, Captains Hendrik Korenaar, Stephanus de La Roche, and Ulrich Hemmingson, Lieutenants Anthonij Johannes van Berglijk, Josephus Maximilliaan Constants, Cornelis de Rot, Jan Fredrik Vieravond, Jan Mijerhoff, and Alexander van Manheim. In conformity with what was resolved today in the council of policy, the war council being convoked by the others, the oath appointed for that purpose was taken by the members thereof and secretary Jan. Java East Coast dated 25 August 1741. After which the president posed the question whether, in view of the Chinese and further Javanese rabble that have entrenched themselves in the encampments and fortifications that have been thrown up around this place as well as Caligawe, Surabaya, etc., daily strengthening and fortifying themselves more and more, it is not highly necessary to attack them with the presently available Europeans and inland militia and, if possible, to destroy them. So it was unanimously decided in the affirmative, and that for this purpose without the least delay all ammunition of war and equipment shall have to be prepared, provided that the captains and lesser officers of the inland militia are summoned to appear in assembly, with the notification that it has been deemed good to first attack the aforementioned encampment and subsequently the aforementioned fortifications, but that each person shall have to report to the Bergopman Steinmets how many men from Java East Coast dated 25 August 1741 stand without their command, in order to form a division thereof, so that the lodging is not left without assistance (in case of unexpected attack by the rebels). All of which has been carried out. Semarang and council dated aforesaid (was signed) A. Roos.

text_translated_detailed: August 1741. From Java's Coast under date of the 25th of August 1741, from Manheim (undersigned, agrees (signed): J. de Haas, per secretary. Report in the form of a day register kept regarding the casualties against the attack of the rebelling Chinese on Java, beginning with the Comptoir [trading post] Samarang on Monday the 21st, yesterday in council of war according to resolution, since most of the war ammunition from the ships lying here at the roadstead had been unloaded and made ready, having been decided this morning early to attack the enemy with the present force of Europeans and native soldiers, such as Balinese, Buginese, Makassarese, Malays, etc., under their leaders both in the kampong and outside against the Chinese. So after the throwing of many bombs and various cannon shots had been carried out, in order to bring the rebels into as much disorder as possible. From Java's Coast under date of the 25th of August 1741, to frighten them off. This effort succeeded around half past five o'clock, under the command of the Mister, when under Nathanael Steinmetsz, Mountain Captain, with four three-pounder metal cannons on the right side at the so-called sharp corner broke into the kampong, Captain Stephanus de la Roche, and on the left side the aforementioned Ulrich Hemmingson with the aforementioned militia, which found the considerable number of Chinese (estimated to be roughly 5,000 strong) in the stone houses, attacked them with courageous fury and bravery and without the least pause fired upon them until mid-morning at ten o'clock, when the enemy, after offering us valiant resistance, nevertheless had to take flight from the aforementioned kampong toward the Passeboen [uncertain: place name] and southern road as well as across the west side of the river through the heavy beams and trees thrown up by them as barriers and banana plants, and thus the said kampong for Coast under date of the 25th of August

The enemy conquered and planted with garrison necessarily under the supervision of a command of senior officers must be guarded, to prevent that the rebels therein can gain no foothold again. So it is, as we are not provided with sufficient senior officers, it has been resolved by a pair to promote their demonstrated vigilance to Captains: the Lieutenants Anthonij Johannes Berg Eijk and Maximiliaan Constants, and to Lieutenants the Ensigns Christiaen Benjamin Rhenert and Jan Andries van Hohendorff, likewise, to Ensigns the Sergeants Iacobus Verbeek, Pieter Brouwer, Willem Ringel Maan and Pieter Arnje, as well as the Ensign of the Native Burgher Corps Carel Carelsz to Lieutenant, the old Batavian Ensign Abraham Fransz, under enjoyment of rations, to restore to his former employment, and finally P. the Bailiff Lieutenant Caijer to Java's Coast under date 25 August 1741 Captains, of which arrangement respectful notice shall be given to their High Excellencies, and their favorable approbation hereupon shall be requested. Your letters of the 13th and 20th of this month I have had the honor to receive well, together with such European soldiers and medicines as it has pleased your High Excellency, Great and Esteemed to graciously send from here for the strengthening of this place, for which I hereby have my humble and obliged thanks to express. Regarding your High Excellency, Great and Esteemed, honored requisition concerning the gathering of rice or paddy [unhusked rice:], which by our natives should occur, is not well feasible. From Java's East Coast under date 25 August 1741, because already the lower fields have been cut, and most of the paddy has been carried upward by the Javanese, which, as it was stored low in the village, the Javanese or Chinese have burned, so that the little which lies stacked in the field is daily gathered by our people, which for them for one or two months can serve as food, which I have also promised to pay them, having thus far provided them no rations but only at their request paid out two months' wages, which request shall have your High Excellency's, Great and Esteemed, approbation, also humbly requesting to be permitted to know whether I may provide them with subsistence money according to their request, if the Javanese would be willing. Thus everything here would be in peace and quiet, since the Chinese are advancing their journey to the east, being already halfway. Samarang, but the contrary appears, since they not only the Chinese turn back

text_translated_detailed: received 30 August 1781. Under the general letter from Java's East Coast under date 25 August 1741. To His High Excellency the High Esteemed Lord Adriaen Valckenier, Governor-General and the Esteemed Lords Councillors of the Netherlands Indies. High Esteemed, strict, great esteem: Secret, earnest, manly, wise, most generous and widely commanding Lord and well-esteemed gentlemen. This serving beforehand in connection with my most recent humble letter of the 14th of this month, I have the honor hereby to note that with great respect I received your High Excellency's great esteem's venerated secret missive of the 15th thereof, wherein besides an original Javanese missive directed to the Madurese Pangerang [Javanese title] Ade Pattij Tsjacraningrat [uncertain: proper name], which shall be attended to at the earliest opportunity, meanwhile the received translations shall serve for information and the brigantine Rotte to meet, as when the present goods from Java's East Coast under date 25 August 1741 shall also be attended to. In the meantime I shall not fail to obey the contents of the aforementioned letter regarding the expected 200 muskets and the cannon, as well as to communicate to the prince what comes to pass concerning the war. By common letter under the same date and its attachments it has appeared that the Company's weapons had gained victory from a changing fire, whereby the militia gave particular proofs of bravery, and principally among the natives the Captain Dain Mabella, who with his people as a lion attended the battle and routed the enemy. I have the honor in the continuation of this to advise that there is still no use to be made of the Samarang [Semarang] Gorbaijs and Goemulaks peoples, as they are scattered like sheep without a shepherd, and it is to be sustained that their leaders collude with the Chinese from Java's East Coast under date 25 August 1741, or at least that they are unable to keep their subjects together.

Furthermore, the orders of the Company are that we should proceed to Tagal in order to suppress the rebellious Chinese, but not in order to kill the Javanese, but at present the Javanese find themselves among the Chinese, therefore we let the Emperor know that the other nations have already rendered service to the Company from Java's East Coast under date the last [day] of August 1740, as there are those from Palembang, Tambai, Malays, Manang, Kabo, those from Aceh, Johor, those from Banjar and Solok, and those from Manding, Danro, as well as those from Kaili, Mandar, likewise the Bugis and Makassarese, and especially the Ambonese, as well as those from Ternate and Tidore, Bima, Sumbawa, Salaiyer, and Tembora, who have all presented their service to the Company, want no wages, as long as they may have the rice, this is what they have truly requested from the Company, and also those from Madura, Sumanap, and Pamakassan have already come to join the Company, therefore may your Highness be mindful to consider the matter well, when Pangerang Aria Mastaram, Pangerang Pura, Baija, and Pangerang Dje Pasanta and Pangerang Panagara from Java's East Coast under date the last [day] of August 1740, with God's grace, Pangerang Blado, who have all risen up against the Company, have been able to surrender against their weapons and have been defeated only by those from Batavia, how would it go now when there are so many other powers who want to oppose the Company, if each now brings only a thousand men, how much would it not amount to, when they have each promised four to five thousand men to the Company; we let all of this be known to the Emperor, besides the power of the Company consisting in its servants who are arriving daily. Ended [and] understood. Translated and certified by me [signed:] J. E. LeBeck. —. Van Jongst gesonden van batavia welke oorlogs ammunitie verhoppe door VE adjude verder mag besorgd werden, ter wijle het selve strekt tot een Preuve van haar hoog Edelens geneegentheit aan welgen: Pangerang on vertussen is mijn begeer dat VE voorn bodem gelieve te provideeren, met soveel rijst olij en andere benodigtheeden als bemagtigd konnen werden, ter welker eijnde de nodige Contanten mede volgen Ik wil geensints twijffelen aan VEviqulantie daar omtrend, temeer dE persoan om't hert van dE Comp legd, van welk een en ander de behoorlyke kennisse is gegeven aanden Pange rang ade Pattij Tjavinengrat al wat ik voor dese keer te seggen heb staat vervat in desen brief die gesz: is ten hoofd Comptoir Samarang den 7. september 1741 /onderstond/ accordeert /getekend/ PL barenclauw secretaris
text_translated_detailed: Java's East Coast, dated the 12th of September 1744. From the voices understood, the interested parties mentioned therein are to be allowed to proceed according to its form and content, saving every good right. Semarang, in council, dated as aforesaid, signed: A. Roos, Nathanael Steimmetsz, K. Koorenaar, Sibens, I. M. V. der Heyden, H. Jan Neman Junior, and R. de Clercq. Undersigned, agreed, was signed: P. L. Baren, S. Cauw, secretary. To the council, Tommangong Soera Diningrat, regent until Sidaijoe, the aforementioned letter-bearer, the ship Karssenhof, has taken in here 15 pieces of metal cannons and 203 muskets in service of Your Excellency, Pangerang, father of the Adipati Tseja Craningrat. Java's East Coast, dated the 13th of September 1744. Recently sent from Batavia, which war ammunition is hoped to be further provided by Your Excellency's adjutant, in the meantime it is my desire that Your Excellency will be pleased to provision the aforementioned vessel with as much rice, oil, and other necessities as can be obtained, for which purpose the necessary cash also follows. I will not doubt Your Excellency's diligence in this regard, all the more so since the person lies at the heart of the Company, of which and all else proper notice has been given to the Pangerang, the Adipati Tjavinengrat. All that I have to say for this time is contained in this letter, which is signed at the head office of Semarang on the 7th of September 1741. Undersigned, agreed, signed: P. L. Baren Clauw, secretary.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast, dated the 15th of August 1744. Cheribon. To the Commandant Justus van Biesum, resident, together with the council. Considering that we here have been so pressed by the Chinese cannon fire that no provisions can be obtained, it is our desire that by Your Excellency everything that can be named from there, even if it were also rice, be procured for the account of the Company and for the refreshment of our inspectors, for which purpose the Chaloup Concordia departs, whom Your Excellency can, having been projected further, dispatch to Tagal in order to take along the natives camping there, sent from Batavia, with which under friendly greetings we remain. Undersigned: Your Excellency's willing friends, signed: A. Roos, Nathanael Steinmetsz, H. Koorenaar. (Siebens, Tonneman Junior, and P. de Clercq in the margin.) Semarang, the 7th of September 1741. Nadien ij in onse vergadering heeden morgen hebben goed gevonden VE te de pecheren naar sidaijoe med een brief Jaar aan den regent aldaer had den Tommangong Soeradiningrat ten eijnde rijst olij Cadjang boonen, gedraagde vis en andere Leevens middelen in te koppen door sijn adjude zynde VE mede gegeeven 4000. rd:s rigte deesen tot VE narigt dat voorn Graan in die Contraijnen wel pleegd te bemagtigen weesen voor 18. a 20 rd:s het last, dog bij aldien den prijs van dien door dese troubel Somwijlen soude gestijgerd weesen werden VE gequalificeerd daar voor temogen betalen het geene dan werd g'Eijscht en voor te bekomen is 8 niet twijffelende of VE sComp intresse sal behertigen, med verder advertentie dat bij aldien VE komt te ondervinden Van Javas Oost Cust onder dato 13:' br: 1741. dat den insaam ter voorsz Plaatse opulent is van Voorsd'eetwaren sal VE illoco daar van per een inlands vaartuijg kennisse moeten geeven, ten eynde Chaloupen afCantings na derwaarts te kunnen senden niet meer Contanten en ter afhaal van voors producten, terwyle VE als dan aldaer sal dienen blijven leggen tot dat den keijser van het Jaar een langer verblijf niet wil verlaten Samarang den 4. Iber 1741. /getekend/ A: Roas. /onderstond accordt /getek p L: baren Clauw secrets Instructie voor den Cappitain maximiliaen Canstans, en onder Coop:l Reijnier de Clerk Aangesien alhier gebrek van rijst te bedugten en te presumeeren is dat te Jnlandse vaartuijgen in de rivieren en op dese rheede leggende negotie drijven med voorn: Graan tot prejuditie van de Comp: So werden VE: gelast alle paartuigen te visiteeren sonder Van Iavas Oost Cust onder dato 13: 7ber:
text_translated_detailed: Java's East Coast, dated the 13th of September 1741. Instructions for the skipper Lodewijk Godskalk, sailing the Company's vessel Karssenhof, standing at his departure to Sidaijoe. Since you in our meeting this morning have seen fit for Your Excellency to proceed to Sidaijoe with a letter to the regent there, the Tommangong Soeradiningrat, for the purpose of purchasing rice, oil, cadjan beans, dried fish, and other provisions, through his adjutant, Your Excellency has also been given 4,000 rixdollars [modern equivalent: Dutch East India Company currency]. I direct this to Your Excellency for your information, that the aforementioned grain in those regions is accustomed to be obtained for 18 to 20 rixdollars per last [modern equivalent: a unit of measurement for grain], but if the price of the same should be raised by this trouble, you are qualified to pay what is then demanded and to be obtained. Do not doubt that Your Excellency will look after the Company's interest, with further notice that if Your Excellency comes to discover at the aforementioned place that the supply of the aforementioned foodstuffs is abundant, you shall there give notice thereof by means of an inland vessel, so that chaloupes from the trading posts can be sent there with not more cash and for the collection of the aforementioned products, while you shall then remain lying there until the emperor of the year will not allow a longer stay. Semarang, the 4th of September 1741. Signed: A. Roos. Undersigned, agreed, signed: P. L. Baren Clauw, secretary. Instructions for the Captain Maximiliaen Canstans and under-Commandant Reinier de Clerk. Considering that a shortage of rice is to be feared and presumed here, and that inland vessels lying in the rivers and on this roadstead are conducting trade with the aforementioned grain to the prejudice of the Company, you are ordered to visit all vessels without [text continues].

Samarang, 4 September 1741 /signed A Raos. undersigned/ agrees /signed/ P L: Baron Clauw secrets. Translation of Javanese letter written by the Pangerang ade pattij Tscraningrat from Madura to the esteemed Mr. Abraham Roos, chief merchant and governor along Java's north coast to Samarang, received 7 September 1741. After customary preamble, I bring to your attention that through my subordinate the Ingabaij Parra djiwa, a missive from their High Excellencies has been delivered to me, in which it is stated that they have sent me as a present 5 pieces from Java's East Coast under date 13 September 1741, metal cannons 200 pieces, muskets with powder and ammunition, which are still at Samarang, therefore I request that the same may be sent as quickly as possible. /undersigned/ translated by me /signed/ J: Leseneur p.l. Translator. Lower [section] agrees /signed/ P L Baron Clauw secret. To the Pangerang ade pattij Tsjacraningrat at Madura. After customary preamble, my brother, now returning envoys have delivered to me a letter whereby you come to request the muskets and cannons sent by their High Excellencies, to which the Esteemed [one] in answer must serve that the same were brought from Batavia only a few days ago and are now stored in the ship Kerssenhoff, which vessel is destined for Sidaijoe, to the end that from Java's East Coast under date 13 September 1747, the 15 pieces of metal cannons and 28 muskets mentioned in the enclosed original missive from their High Excellencies to you, prescribed by your son the Radeen Tommangon Soeradiningrat, be further provided, as well as that through his care the Company may be supplied with rice and other necessities
