text_translated_detailed:
From Java's East Coast dated 13 September 1741, the bearers of this letter are Sergeant Jan Ternosseij with 6 native soldiers. We request Your Excellency that the aforementioned sergeant may be retained provisionally, as he is one of the most cunning ringleaders. Furthermore, Sergeant Jan Ternofskij, having just fallen from the steps of the guard, broke his arm, and in his place the quartermaster Willem Lemkens was employed as substitute. Approved and signed by P.L. Baron Clauw, Secretary.

Translation of a Javanese letter written by the Radeen Tommangong Tsjacraningrat, chief regent over the Company's lands of Sumanap and Pamacassan, together with his guardian Radeen Aijoe Soeradiningrat, to the Honorable Mr. Benjamin Blom, Captain and chief at Surabaya, received there on 18 August and delivered at Samarang on 6 September 1741.

From Java's East Coast dated 13 September 1741.

After customary preamble: Through the soldier Gerrit Nedak, a letter has been handed to me from which I understand that Lieutenant Ismail with five vessels, according to Your Excellency's supposition, has fled to the island of Antalangoe, which belongs to the district of Sumanap. Therefore, Your Excellency has been pleased to order me to cross to the aforementioned island with my subjects provided with their weapons, and upon encountering the aforementioned Ismail, to allow him and his companions to be killed, which shall be properly carried out. Translated by me. Signed I. Lefreur, translator. Approved and signed P.L. Baron Clauw, Secretary.

One sergeant and two aforementioned soldiers have appeared here with a letter, from whose contents I understand that Your Excellencies have been pleased to accede to their request to depart for Batavia, and in place of the aforementioned Mr. Bartholomeus Visscher, who was summoned there as governor, to appoint Mr. Roos here, who on the 4th of this month was presented to the people. text_translated_detailed:
His guardian Radeen Aria Soeradiningrat and her husband Radeen Aria Soeradiningrat.

After customary preamble.

Furthermore, this serves to inform Your Excellency that the Lieutenant of the Macassarese from Java's East Coast, dated 13 October 1741, Intje Ismail van Griple, has put to sea yesterday night with 5 vessels, but where he has gone is still unknown to me. Suspecting that they may have turned their course to the island of Tolangon in order to gain some accomplices there, so that he might better carry out his intended wicked plan. And since the Company's land of Sumanap could also be disturbed thereby, it is therefore necessary to watch everywhere, and particularly at Tolangon, not to regard him alone, but to see him and his adherents captured alive or dead in hand, for it is of the highest necessity that this harmful scoundrel be stopped. The bearer of this is the soldier Gerrit Niedag. All that I have to say for this time is contained in this letter, which is written at the Dutch Comptoir Surabaya on 11 August, signed in the year 1741.

From Java's East Coast, dated 13 September 1741.

P. Blom. Approved and signed P.L. Baron Clauw, Secretary.

Surabaya, to the Merchant Vincent van Wingaerden, chief, together with the Radeen titled.

Very much grieved have we seen from Your Excellency's letter of the first of this month the death of Merchant Blom, the disorder of Surabaya's garrison, and the fourth quarrel between Your Excellency and the council at Passourouang. To which we shall answer in advance that good command exercised by you can bring a disordered militia to reason, especially when their officers set a good example before them. You can meanwhile not be assisted with any Europeans, given that the greatest power of the enemy has us surrounded and the garrison here is weak. Meanwhile, we shall not abandon ourselves to the aforementioned quarrels, but recommend to you to observe our previous orders, since unity.

From Java's East Coast dated 13 September 1741, is presently necessary for the strengthening of the Company's weapons and can remove the stone of offense from the way.

The enclosed letter shall you cause to be delivered at the earliest to the Radeen Tommangong Tsja. Cranagara and his guardian, whose Dutch translation you can consult for information. From this you shall see that the aforementioned regent is instructed to provide more people for the Company's service under the command of capable officers. Thus you shall be obliged to provide the Comptoir Passourouang with the necessary manpower, gunpowder, and lead, of which the aforementioned you recently received a generous portion. The request of Sergeant Dirk Roelofsz to be promoted to ensign, we shall present on occasion to Her High Excellencies. The further contents of your letter, mentioned for communication, have been received, and principally with respect to the 6 cannons, which to the Madurese Prince, at his request, from Java's East Coast dated 13 September in the year 1741, have been given over, as not being convenient to us.

Translation of Javanese letter written by the Tumenggung Tjacranagara, head regent over the Company's lands Sumanap and Pamacassan, likewise from Java's East Coast under date 13th September, Year 1741 his guardians regent Aijoe Soeradiningrat and her husband regent Soeradiningrat, to the Honored, esteemed Lord Abraham Roos, chief merchant and governor on and along Java's North East Coast, at Semarang. Received the 6th December 1741. After customary preamble, Your Excellency, I beg you to send a letter from which I have seen that it has pleased their High Excellencies to appoint Your Excellency as governor of Java in place of the Lord Bartholomeus Piescher, who has been summoned to Batavia, through which notification I express my thanks, while I have presented the people to Your Excellency according to custom. Furthermore, so I have, according to Your Excellency's command, had Surabaya strengthened with half the inhabitants of Sumanap and Pamacassan under the command of regent Pourwadiningrat and manconagara. Your Excellency has instructed me from Java's East Coast under date 13th September 1741 further to order Pasuruan to be provided with people, which I shall likewise comply with, sending Marta Nagara, Demang Soeradigoena Ranga Cartabasa and Marta Widjaja from Sumanap, likewise from Pamacassan admangara, Cattadjaza Tanda Nitiesastea

text_translated_detailed: The inland officers brought to us a free Javanese woman, a dependent of the Macassar, Dain Mangabaij, who, when carefully interrogated, related that a few days ago she, together with a Javanese dependent of the aforementioned Dani Mangabeij, was captured by the hostile Javanese on the road to the coastal village of Janebij, and from there was brought to the regent Tsiestra Soema, who had taken his residence from the Company's salt mill on Java's East Coast, dated the 13th of December 1741, was brought according to the aforementioned agreement, and she, the dependent, was placed in chains in good custody. However, she had managed to escape. She also reported having seen that a large number of Chinese and Javanese were gathering there to erect two plantations of coconut palms. Furthermore, she had heard that recently six pieces of cannon had been obtained from the enemy, and that preparations were being made for this. Whether and insofar as this report corresponds with the truth is unknown to us due to the lack of other good spies. Therefore we here merely add for communication that the rebels have made a palisade on the east side of this mountain of the forest across the rice fields, and on the west side likewise something similar, from where they daily position themselves with a good number of armed men to draw toward us and shoot at our men who must fetch the fresh water below at the foot of the mountain. Received the 19th of September 1741 from Java's East Coast dated the 13th of September 1741, and since this is the only well that still remains, it becomes increasingly difficult to obtain the necessary water. For the rest, having nothing else to write, we break off and under the wish of the Lord's precious blessings have the honor to sign ourselves with deep respect. [Below:] Title. [Below:] Your Excellency's most humble servants. [Signed:] R. Engelink and L. Leepeltak. [In margin:] Japara the 3rd of September 1741. [Below:] Agreed. [Was signed:] P.L. Barenclauw, Secretary.

text_translated_detailed: Lands Tommogong Wieracestra. Customary preamble. With great difficulty have I awaited an opportunity to be able to give Your Excellency some proof of the care with which the Company, Your Excellency, and his Majesty, the other regents, are surrounded by my true affection toward you. And since I understand from the Captains Dain Mabella and Intje Boesong that Your Excellency is inclined to appear here, let it be testimony from me regarding this, and I declare that Your Excellency and his subjects shall suffer no harm, remaining as surety or as hostages for the aforementioned Captains. Thus I hope that Your Excellency will come here at the earliest, so that I may assure myself that Your Excellency is a sincere and well-meaning friend of the Company. When this is embraced, Your Excellency shall be treated as a member of the bond of friendship and crowned with a rich reward. Your faithful service is valued. What I have to say for this time is contained in this letter, which is written at the head office Samarang on the 4th of September in the year 1741. [signature mark] Agrees [signed] S Paeren Clauw Secretary. From Java's East Coast under date the 13th of September 1741. To the Lands Tommangong Tirtawigoena at Cartasoera [Kartasura]. Customary preamble. By this means my brother makes known that the Tommangong Wiera Testra of Damak is inclined to appear here, to which I have agreed, presuming that through this means the desired friendship between me and the Susuhunan's Regents shall grow, and that the old peace shall be renewed. And since I persuade myself that his Majesty will be pleased with this, when it is presented to him with good intentions, I trust that Your Excellency will present the foregoing to his Highness in such a manner that his Majesty takes no offense at it. All that I have to say for this time is contained in this letter, which is written at the head office Samarang on the 4th.

And we by council resolution solely because of a meager supply of Gunpowder and encirclement by the enemy for the most part, in hope that Your Esteemed Honors will not take it amiss for the stated reasons that we refrain from firing cannon or musket shots. Regarding the drinking water we refer to our previous letter, since this further serves as escort for a Javanese named Balie belonging to the chaloup of the Macassar free burgher Mattheus Tourein, who departed from this roadstead some days ago toward Macassar, which aforementioned young man was brought here this afternoon by the Malays and interrogated by us, related that he some days ago with his companion had been seized by the Chinese and subsequently brought to the Company's sawmill, and there by order of the Adipati Tsitra Soema had been put in chains, and that they had now managed to break loose and escape, that his companion had become separated from him on the way & further after Java's South Coast under Date 16th September 1741.

text_translated_detailed: the Council. Title. On the 11th of this our last, to which we respectfully refer, From Java's East Coast under date 16th of September 1741, we only add thereby that yet another bastion has been erected by the enemy on this mountain against the sort of the Lodge over, so that this further serves as an accompaniment to the one and three monthly papers, namely a Subsidy roll of the youngest passed three months, the short strength of the garrison under the Company's August, [uncertain: abbreviation] of the Company's inland servants, a small receipt roll of the Extraordinary provisions, a name roll of the deceased and likewise of their death debts. While a declaration of the under-officers regarding the here-lying yacht the Christinasophia has been delivered to us by the commander of that vessel for the disposition of Your Honour, likewise passes over. In the meantime we request that if it should please Your Honour, that vessel be ordered to Samarang before we may obtain another in its place, since this is of the utmost necessity, in order to defend the enemy from this strand on the east side of this mountain from Java's East Coast under date 16th of September 1741, or at least to make the work there as much as possible dangerous and difficult and to secure passage. To which latter end it would also be of no lesser usefulness if Your Honour could send one or two chaloups [small boats] hereward to alarm the enemy who has already made works on the west cape and brings them daily closer, and as much as is feasible therein. In which hope we conclude and after respectful greeting remain with all respect and regard, Your Honour's obedient servants, R. Engelink S. Lepeltak. In the margin: Japara the 13th of September 1741. Agrees, I. Bieles E.g. Clerk.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast under date 16th of September 1741. Batavia to His Honour the High and Noble Lord Adriaan Valckenier, Governor-General, and Noble Lords, Councillors of the Netherlands Indies. Title. This serving beforehand as an accompaniment to the duplicate of my recently respectful letter to Your High Noble and esteemed Honour of the date 13th of this month, I have the honour to communicate a copy of a letter written by the under-corporal and Tagalog resident Laurens Grothe of the 11th before, addressed to me and the council, and this should be noted in the common letter, but since therewith are annexed a Javanese and Malay letter of great importance, I shall let the same follow here beside, the aforementioned letter of the inland content being that the resident on military matters cannot transport hereward, for the reason that they are not only needed in order to provide sustenance and to protect this office against all unexpected attacks of the enemy. From Java's East Coast under date 16th of September 1741, but also to be able to lead them when the Company were attacked, the more to be feared was that the Susuhunan through a granted mandate (of which more shall be mentioned hereafter) would be able to make himself master of the Company's inland servants, thus to keep the aforementioned office safe and out of danger, it is deemed necessary to let the inland people remain there, with humble weak request that the garrison be reinforced with the utmost speed, while besides this cannot be carried out as aforesaid. It is manifest therein that the Susuhunan has urged all the Company's both European and inland servants, and in particular the last-mentioned, to leave the Company, and thereupon to surrender themselves to the discretion and promised pardon of His Majesty, since they could not be regarded as enemies but rather as the Dutch Company. text_original: Van Javas Oost Cust onder dato 16:' Sept: 1741. Hoog Edele groote agtb: gants onderdanige Engehoorsame dienaer /:was getekent:/ R Roos /in margine/ Samarang den 16:' 7ber: 1741 (nog Lager:/ P: S: Naa het teeckenen deses ontfing ik Een Iavaanse ola door Soesoesoenangs regenten den Tommangong Wiera Goera en Radeen Ingabij marta Soera gesz: aan den Paleijs vaandrig Batjoe En nalawang sa waarbij deselve door Iaar ginciteerd werden om den soezoehoenang te Gehoorsamen ende Compareeren aan dewestkant vande groote baviaan, Vermits zij voorgenomen hebben Samarang te attacqueeren nader Consteerende bij in Closa Copia Translaat Samarang aan den Edele agtb: Heer R: Roos oppercoopman Engesag hebber op En Langs Iavas Noord oost Cust, benevens den Raad Van Javas Oost Cust onder dato 16:' 7ber: 1741 agtb: veed g'eerde letteren van den 5: deeser sijn mijn behoorlijk ter hand gesteld, en gaak ingevalle VEd agtb: g' eerde ordre Hier nev:s den Traijer Jacob Pikkelman g'accompagneerd Jan Hendrik door den Sergeank Cramer en Corporaal Cornelis Sijnagel, op welkers geddag niet veel te noemen valk, ookgaat op sijn versoek over den Indigomaeker Leopold Jochemsz: op Tacalougan bescheijden den 7: deeser ontfing de Tesamentlijke inlandse Capitains alhier een brief vanden soesoehoenang hier nevens in Copia met het antwoord van gem: Captitains 't welke hoope van VEd: approbatie zal sijn, uijt gende letteren sul VEd: agtb: ook consteeren ten de insentie vanden keijzer, en zol noodsakelijk die inlandse magt alheer gerequireerd word, in gevalle men dese Plaats niet wil sacrificeeren betuijgende bij aldien ik niet meerder als 5OO:wen mag Behouden onder 100. zieken En gequesten waar Van Javas Oost Cust onder dato 16: Septemb: 1741 souden zyn, ik niet in vertaarden, deese Post dierondsom opperlegd te kunnen bewaren vermits dat seer apparent is, dat ik in het korte niet alleen door de Iavanen Sal be: ceegerd
text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast under date 16th September 1741. Most High and Noble, greatly esteemed: entirely your obedient and humble servant [was signed:] R. Roos [in margin] Semarang, the 16th of September 1741 (further below:) P.S. After signing this, I received a Javanese letter through the Susuhunang's regent, the Tommangong Wiera Goera and Radeen Ingabij Marta Suera, sent to the Palace ensign Batjoe and Nalawang Sa, whereby they were incited by him to obey the Susuhunang and appear at the west side of the great ravine, since they have intended to attack Semarang. Further confirming this in Close Copy Translation, Semarang to the Noble and esteemed Mister R. Roos, chief merchant and inspector on and along Java's Northeast Coast, together with the Council From Java's East Coast under date 16th September 1741. Esteemed: Your Worship's much valued letters of the 5th of this month have been properly delivered to me, and I shall proceed, in case Your Worship's esteemed order [is given]. Herewith the prisoner Jacob Pikkelman, accompanied by Jan Hendrik, through Sergeant Cramer and Corporal Cornelis Sijnagel, regarding whose conduct there is not much to mention, also proceeds at his request over the indigo maker Leopold Jochemsz. at Tacalougan. On the 7th of this month, the testamentary inland Captains here received a letter from the Susuhunang, herewith in Copy, with the answer of the aforementioned Captains, which I hope will have Your Worship's approval. From the enclosed letters, Your Worship will also ascertain the intention of the Emperor, and it will necessarily be required that the inland force here be called upon, in case one does not wish to sacrifice this place, showing that if I may not retain more than 500 men under 100 sick and wounded, from Java's East Coast under date 16th September 1741, I would not hesitate to be able to preserve this post in the meantime, since it is very apparent that in the short term I shall not only be besieged

text_translated_detailed: of the Emperor, and it will necessarily be required that the inland force here be called upon, in case one does not wish to sacrifice this place, showing that if I may not retain more than 500 men under 100 sick and wounded, from Java's East Coast under date 16th September 1741, I would not hesitate to be able to preserve this post in the meantime, since it is very apparent that in the short term I shall not only be besieged by the Javanese, but also that the enemy, not being able to hold out any longer at Semarang, would not go eastward but would withdraw in this direction. Since this post is not yet so very much troubled, it is nevertheless disputed; the Javanese [have] our people six rice warehouses, and if their force permits it, they would certainly commit more hostilities. This is accompanied by a name roll of the inland military here, and two general receipts for two months' wages for their reinforcement, to the amount of rix-dollars nine thousand one hundred thirty-two, as well as two death rolls, together with a short [uncertain: original text] and subsidy roll, all according to the enclosed register. With which this shall conclude under the wish that God's precious goodness [will be upon us]. text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast dated 16th September 1741, it is [understood:] Title [Lower:] Your Excellency's most humble and obedient [servant] was signed Tagal the 11th [7ber:] 1741 [in margin [Lower stood:] agrees [signed:] [Deeler E: g: Clercq Translation of Malay letter Received by the Captain of the Native Nation to be delivered to the Susuhunan Pakubuwono & his Court, residing in Kartasura, [uncertain: adimii grax]. After the preamble, Your Excellency's letter has been delivered to us in this Land, whose contents we have understood. Since Your Excellency has been pleased to order us to return to Batavia, how can this be accomplished when our houses and all that is ours have been burned by the Chinese? From Your Excellency's writings it has also come to our attention that Your Excellency's matter has been the cause of the Company's expenses being brought upon your subjects to 1395 From Java's East Coast dated 16th September 1741. A heavy burden, which however does not seem to be true. Please consider, Good Company, Your Majesty's [involvement] in the Surabaya war has assisted, whereby many of our Brothers have had to lose their lives. Therefore the Company not without reason seeks its suffered damage to be recovered. In that it should be assumed that the Company has supported it with all its strength. So Your Excellency has found that the Company's expenses weighed heavily upon your subjects, why then should this be made known by letters, Your Excellency forbids us to [support] the Company ourselves and Your Excellency in case of need, but we are not inclined to do so, nor shall the Chinese, who are the ruiners of the Land, enjoy any such thing from us. The Company's order is to capture them and kill them, but to disturb [things] with the Javanese so that the Land is laid waste, is the Javanese's fault from Java's East Coast dated 16th [7ber:] 1741, who have mingled themselves with the Chinese. We make

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast dated 10th September 1741. Since we have resolved to conquer Semarang, we hereby make known to you, your Inclination of the Susuhunang, together if so. You shall have to come to me, for I pledge myself, not only for you but for all the Saleijers, Bugineese and Macassarese. I hope to obtain an answer hereupon within one or two days, or else to meet you myself. My camp is situated on the west side of the great Davian in the negory Padzagalan. [Undersigned:] Translated by me. [Signed:] J. Sesieur, P.r translator. [Lower:] Agrees. [Was signed:] J. Bielier, Esq. Clerk. Batavia to His Excellency the High and Noble Gentleman Adriaan Valckenier, Governor General and well-esteemed Gentlemen Councillors of the Dutch Indies. Received 27th September 1741. From Java's East Coast dated 16th September 1741. Your High and Noble Esteemed Lordship. In accordance with Your High and Esteemed Order of the 6th of this month, regarding the inland [matters], I have sent five hundred and nine soldiers by sea from Pier to Cheribon, which these Javanese, who certainly have their pioneers there, namely, have now arrived, being much more assured for this reason. Coming daily are parties of 30 to 40 who depart to near this Lodge, to see if they could capture any people, and I am also making again Bentings and Dalf miles from here. From Your High and Noble Esteemed Lordship, much esteemed Letters of the 14th of this month. Yesterday when I came ashore, I had the honor to perceive Your Worship's High and Noble Esteemed satisfaction regarding the letter which the Joint Inland Captains from here have written to the Susuhunang, which I shall also make known to them, and they promised the Company always, and in all respects the [loyalty] from Java's East Coast under date 16th September 1741 to remain faithful. So that to them all the more to encourage, in hope of favorable well-being I take the liberty to present to Your Worship's High and Noble Esteemed Lordship, according to request. Namely, to grant me some whom the Company has already served in various expeditions. Whether from Java or from the Malabar, [I request] to be able to obtain positions according to the enclosed register. The chief surgeon Casparus van Iel, together with the two assistant surgeons Gerrit Hendriksz and Jan Dan, have arrived here, and have also examined the medicines, and respectfully request through Your High and Noble Esteemed Lordship that the accompanying Petition may be granted. The master Jan Hendrik Schreuder having died here on the 10th of this month. The ship Velsen, through lack of provisions, no longer being able to hold out, now goes to receive [supplies]. 27th September 1741. From Java's East Coast dated 16th September 1741. Furthermore, on this occasion consideration was given to the continual disposition of some members of this assembly, for whose strengthening Captains Gerrit Mom and Hendrik Baule were elected and at the same time introduced. Moreover, consideration was taken of the petition made by the humble chief surgeon Mattheus Haartmans here present, in order to be transferred from Java's east coast under date 30th September 1741 to Batavia, on account of his weak bodily constitution and other ailments. It has therefore been deemed good to agree to this, and in his place, with favorable approval of their High Excellencies, to appoint the chief transport master Josephus Bolee, as well as to replace him with the second transport master Jan Deput at ƒ50 [Dutch guilders], together with the surgeon Christoffel Loerig at ƒ40, since they were noted to possess the required capacity and vigilance. Whereas from the esteemed letter of their High Excellencies dated 29th August of this year it was established that there is a great shortage of all panjallang vessels, contingent vessels, and other craft there, together with the granted qualification for the purchase thereof, so in fulfillment of their High Excellencies' esteemed requisition, it has been decided unanimously that the vessels lying here at the roadstead and belonging to various Chinese, from Java's east coast under date 30th July 1741, shall be inventoried by the secretary in the presence of expressly appointed commissioners, and the same shall be remitted at the first convenient opportunity for the esteemed disposition of their High Excellencies, the High Indian government at Batavia. On the 13th of this month our last respectful letter was sent to your Esteemed Excellency, to which we refer, so we find ourselves compelled to send this again to bring to your Esteemed Excellency's knowledge that the enemy and from Java's east coast under date 30th July 1741, with their works have approached so far that no one from the Berg can come out of the lodge to the Esteemed Company's residence, and thus all correspondence with the inland officers, who are stationed at the aforesaid Company's residence and the Chinese, has been broken off. Indeed, it is to be feared that those two extended posts, which are attacked day and night by the enemy, and are in the greatest danger, will be lost, especially since the smallness of the garrisons will cause them to be lost, the more so because the rebels have positioned themselves in a palisade behind the Berg such that we cannot assist with cannon from the fortress. Whereby also, moreover, the drinking water—as the most important matter—is now completely cut off from us. text_translated_detailed: —, P: de Veds, and L: Tonneman Junior /:in margin:/ From Java's East Coast under Date 30th July 1741: Semarang, the 25th September, Year 1741. /:below:/ stood/ agrees /:signed:/ P: L Baeren Clouw: secretary; Semarang: To the Esteemed and Honorable Lord Abraham Roos, chief merchant and governor along Java's northeast coast together with the council. Title. Esteemed and Honorable, Your letters of the 23rd of this month have been duly received by us, from which it appears that Your Esteemed Honors have seen fit to order the Chaloup d'Ongesiene [the Unforeseen] with the unexpected change and the peppering warehouse at Semarang to be summoned, for the reason that we have written that we are not in a position to ship timber, and to load those two aforementioned vessels in accordance with Your Esteemed Honors' orders, so it should be noted first that Your Esteemed Honors' commands were not to fill those two aforementioned vessels completely, but rather the Yacht the Christina from Java's East Coast under Date 30th July 1741, Sophia, and on the aforementioned chaloup the unexpected change, and that over this the peppering warehouse here shall only have to remain lying; whereupon we have also been further compelled to show Your Esteemed Honors that a single vessel such as the peppering warehouse, provided with light artillery, was not in a position to keep the sea passage free, and therefore the enemy could also bring no harm whatsoever: — from which our respectful writing then does not appear that the peppering warehouse, when the same remained accompanied by the Yacht the Christina Sophia, would be serviceable here, and in any case further change would likewise be of no utility, as Your Esteemed Honors now see fit to note; on the contrary, we have on the 13th respectfully requested one or two more chaloupes, and this we have repeated again in our most recent letter, wherefore we shall therefore await Your Esteemed Honors' further order from Java's East Coast under Date 30th July 1741; for the

text_translated_detailed: same remained accompanied by the Yacht the Christina Sophia, would be serviceable here, and in any case further change would likewise be of no utility, as Your Esteemed Honors now see fit to note; on the contrary, we have on the 13th respectfully requested one or two more chaloupes, and this we have repeated again in our most recent letter, wherefore we shall therefore await Your Esteemed Honors' further order from Java's East Coast under Date 30th July 1741; for the rest we find ourselves obliged to make known to Your Esteemed Honors that this fortress is in great danger of falling into the hands of the enemy, since their power has not only increased in such a manner that we with our small force of people can accomplish nothing through a sortie, but also that they have constructed a battery a musket shot away from here on the Hill, from which they simultaneously fire with 3 or 4 pieces of heavy cannon, so that the cannonballs fly through our palisades, and they have also already placed 9 pieces of cannon on the seashore on the east side of the hill, which last has been brought to us by a trusted spy, while the enemy on the west side below the hill likewise with heavy cannon are actually firing on our Inlanders [indigenous soldiers] who at the Company's residence and the Chinese street as very necessary posts keep watch from Java's East Coast under Date 30th July 1741, have opened fire, therefore we request the speediest relief or explicit orders according to which we and all circumstances are to proceed, meanwhile we remain, transmitted through the undersigned bookkeeper Joan Renne, with which we close, remaining with all respect and deference /:understood/ Title /:below/ Your Esteemed Honors' willing Servants /:signed:/ R: Engelink, P:r Leepeltak /:in margin/ Japara the 24th July 1741. /:below stood/ agrees /:signed/ Pr Boeden Clouw secretary Semarang, to as before, The chaloup the Unforeseen

text_translated_detailed: from Java's East Coast under date 30th July 1740, yesterday began to fire with heavy cannon 6 lb. iron cannonballs, whereby we shall be compelled, if they continue therein, to sally out with our meager force to overcome their cannon if it is possible, principally because when they come to hit the roof of the house or guard post in the lodge, which is built high of planks and is not covered with tiles, it will be impossible for anyone in this small lodge to remain. In answer to Your Esteemed Honors' missive of the 18th, it should be noted that the barrel of lard, some bacon and the like meat, as well as 200 lb. of nails of various sorts have been duly brought to us, for which shipment we express our thanks to Your Esteemed Honors, directing this likewise in company with the enclosed request letter of the bookkeeper Joan Reune, who is humbly beseeching Your Esteemed Honors for a favorable disposition thereon, while the second undersigned to Your Esteemed Honors in his place is proposed, the here-mentioned soldier Jacob Reesgee, who for a considerable time one after another at the pen has served to great satisfaction, to succeed him, for the obtaining of which his request letter herewith passes to Your Esteemed Honors, and since we testify that he brings complete satisfaction in his service, so we join our request most willingly with his. With which we conclude and remain with respectful greetings, with all respect and deference /:understood/ Title /:below/ Your Esteemed Honors' humble Servant /:was signed:/ R: Engelink and Lamb: Deepeltak, /:beside/ Japara the 21st September, year 1741. /:below stood:/ agrees /:signed/ BoeE S: „ren Clouw: secretary Japara. — From Java's East Coast under Date 30th July 1741. text_translated_detailed: Received on the 19th, September 1741. From Java's south coast, dated the 30th of July 1741. Samarang, the 23rd of September 1741. [undersigned:] Agreed, [signed:] I.L. Baeren Clauw, secretary, Batavia. To His Excellency the highly esteemed and respected Lord Adriaan Valckenier [Adriaan Valckenier:], Governor-General and the well-esteemed Lords, counselors of the Netherlands Indies; Title. My last respectful letters to your Excellency's great esteem have been from the 9th of this month, to which my reverent conduct is such that this letter alone is directed to have the honor to respectfully notify your Excellency's great esteem that, notwithstanding the assurance of the Javanese, as I have had the honor to note to your Excellency in my last letter, they with their force have always had to yield before ours. Excepting yesterday, when our people were again at their fortifications and found that they are now over ten thousand strong, so that they have not only continuously fired from cannons and muskets without wanting to yield a foot, but attempted to encircle our people so that ours had to retreat with the loss of one man and one seriously wounded. Also, the enemies are busy making new fortifications closer to this lodge and have in their service about two hundred Baliers [Baliers: Indonesian warriors] and Bugis [Bugis: Indonesian ethnic group] who have lived on Brebes and Pemarang; these have also called out to our people in their language, "Come here, friends, if you have courage," so that they will certainly come closer and closer. Therefore, I humbly request that I may not only retain the three hundred warriors that your Excellency's great esteem has graciously ordered to be sent to Samarang, but also in case of great necessity, I may request from Cheribon in case they can be spared there.

From Java's south coast, dated the 30th of July 1741, together with the assembled officers who are stationed at Segal [Segal: likely Tegal], to their Excellencies the high Indian Government at Batavia, received on the 19th of September 1741. And in all obedience, we Captain Mohammad Marougin and Ismail, together with the further captains, lieutenants, and ensigns who are stationed at Segal, make known to their Excellencies that we all, in accordance with their Excellency's orders which we received from our predecessor, the Lord Commissioner, namely to pursue the Chinese, have observed without the least negligence, and to give satisfaction regarding this, we have traveled the mountains up and down until we came to Tegal, and at the time that we departed from Brebes, we were on the way observed by the enemy who were two to three thousand strong; nevertheless, we have done our best to comply with the received orders, as we have also done daily at Tegal, where we have been in action several times against the enemy.

From Java, Superintendent of Customs, under date of the 15th of August 1741. Current record kept at the head office of Samarang: Sunday, in the afternoon, in the outer works, a Javanese was found, upon whom, upon being searched, there were found a quantity of thin flintlock bullets and some bamboo tubes with gunpowder, and he was suspected of being a spy of the enemy, wherefore he was locked in the stocks this day. text_translated_detailed: having been entertained to satisfaction by that regent with his sincere and courteous farewell from the governor and the other gentlemen present, they then proceeded to their assigned lodgings. This morning, a letter was further brought by the Malay Kitje from Japara, written by the mountain captain and council there, whereby his arrival was made known, as well as the departure from there of the ship the Dam to Surabaya with more details mentioned in the letter. Wednesday, the 4th of October, there appeared on this roadstead from Cheribon the Chaloup Concordia, from Java, Superintendent of Customs, under date of the 15th of August 1741, which was sent to fetch provisions, also bringing 20 cows and nothing else. During the past night, there was very heavy shooting at our outer posts by the hostile Chinese and Javanese, yet they caused no damage to us. Thursday, the 5th of October, in the morning at 7 o'clock, there was brought to this lodge a Javanese named Soeba Proena from Tanquilang, whose account is to be found at the secretariat. Furthermore, nothing remarkable occurred, except that the enemies are daily strengthening themselves more and more with breastworks, while according to reports all have allied themselves with the Chinese-Javanese shore regents and rebels, and are distributed in fortifications all around Samarang. Friday, the 6th of October, the Pantjallang was dispatched from here, from Java, Superintendent of Customs, under date of the 15th of August 1741, to the east toward Japara with a letter to the mountain captain Steinmersz and the council there. Furthermore, the enemies made little noise this night, and nothing else of note occurred. Saturday, the 7th of October, overnight there appeared at this roadstead the Batavia burgher Jan Samuel Hem with his chaloup, by means of which, according to private reports, the governor Roos has obtained his release from this coast. In his place has been appointed as provisional governor the mountain captain Nathanael Steinmetsz, who on this day has been notified by letter to come as soon as possible to take over the post until further orders from her High Excellencies. Also on this day, there arrived at this roadstead the Chaloup the Unforeseen Changes, the Contingent of the Pepper Garden, which first-mentioned vessel brought a letter from the aforementioned Java, Superintendent of Customs, under date of the 15th of August 1741, to the mountain captain and council at Japara, along with a cargo of timber, to be seen in the accompanying papers. The rebels also fired several shots, and from our works a quantity of bombs and mortar grenades were thrown into their fortifications, supported by heavy and light artillery. Sunday, the 8th of October, nothing occurred except that the enemies, both with heavy and light artillery, continuously fired at our outer works and daily advanced with flying flags and trumpets. Monday, the 9th of October, likewise nothing of note passed, and today the ship Gasperdam again appeared at this roadstead, coming from Tagal with a quantity of rice. Tuesday, the 10th of October, the Pantjallang the Pepper Garden was dispatched from here to Japara, from Java, Superintendent of Customs, under date of the 15th of August 1741, with some war ammunition and a letter to the officials there. Furthermore, shooting continued both from the enemy's works and ours, night and day, since the malcontents are daily strengthened by the native shore dwellers. Wednesday, the 11th of October.

To the valiant mister nath:e Steinmetz: Head of the Company's militia on Java together with the council. Valiant Mister and Friends Your Honor's letter of the first of this month we have received and from it with satisfaction seen that the ship the Dam has been dispatched to Surabaya, also that everything was being done in order to attack the enemies positioned around the mountain in their raised entrenchments and we approve your Honor's disposition concerning the unloading of the iron cannons of 6: lb: and one constable's mate with one sailor from the aforementioned vessel, wishing that the Almighty deign to bless your Honor's weapons for the advantage of the Company and the destruction of the raging enemies; meanwhile we inform your Honor of the requested cash and other goods as specified are on the accompanying bill of lading and invoice, while your Honor is authorized to unload from the ship Beekvliet that lies anchored there such a quantity of rice as is sufficient for one month's rations for the benefit of the 172 heads [modern equivalent: men] that were embarked in the aforementioned ship, likewise to the voluntary European and native servants for extra work daily to be paid as much as is practicable here. with which under friendly greeting we remain /:undersigned/ your Honor's good friends (:was signed/ A: Roos, Gerrit Mom, H: Koorenaar C: sibens, of Java's east coast under Date the 15th: August: 1741. g Tonneman Junior, and R„r De Clerq, /:to the side / Samarang the 4th: August: 1741. /:undersigned/ agrees,

Title. With reference to our most recent letter of the 1st of this month dispatched to your Honor by the mail boat kitjel we hereby inform you in advance that on the second of this month in the morning when we were at the foot of the mountain here busy throwing beams into the river the captain of the Buginese Tosalaurna and a soldier of that company named niengoe campoen, barol were struck by a 6: lb: cannon ball from the lower fortification of the enemy so unfortunately that the first, the right and the last both below at the ankle were shot away, for which reason on the oral reports both from the ship's chief surgeon Pieter van Drielst as well as then in place advised under said Jan van der horst, we have resolved to have an amputation performed on the aforementioned 2 wounded in order, if it were possible, to save their lives, which removal of the first has had the desired effect, but the second died before any beginning could be made with it, finding that captain in a tolerable condition so that there is hope for his recovery, meanwhile we request at the very earliest without delay that with one of the Company's vessels to here be sent a number

text_translated_detailed: Extirpation, as mentioned above: 2: requested to be allowed to happen, if it were possible to save the life of that blind person, which removal of the First Effect has resulted in, but the second, before any beginning could be made with it, passed away, finding that captain in such an intimate disposition so that there is hope for that outcome. Japara To the valiant Mister Nath:s Steinmets, head of the Javanese militia together with the council. Title: The Chaloup d'Unseen Change has here brought your Honor's letter of the 6th instant together with a parcel of timber works of which bill of lading and invoice have been received, and from the aforementioned letter we have seen with satisfaction that the ship Beekvliet likewise lies in loading of the same materials, which vessel can remain at the Coast as long as until another is sent in its place, when the aforementioned ship Beekvliet shall be seen to. From Java's East Coast under Date 15th August 1741. In the meantime we approve the lightening from that vessel and the Yacht Christina Sophia of 6,840 pounds of rice, one barrel of bacon and thereof of meat, meanwhile let it be sent to your Honor in satisfaction of the requisition made, which is specified on the attached bill of lading and invoice and can be spared from our stores. From Java's south coast under Date the 15th of August 1741, the Mountain Commander through the Governor Nathanael Steinmets, made known in council his continued complaint regarding gravel and other sickness which daily diminish his strength and do not allow that his Excellency can be present in person at all works and issue necessary orders in service of the Company in the chain of command, for which reason the aforesaid Excellency Mountain Commander proposed to this assembly whether it would not be deemed good that the Captain Gerrit Mom, who has shown himself inclined thereto, be adjunged to him as substitute, likewise the ensign Jacobus Verbeek as his adjutant, in order also to keep watch over what is given and performed and to command thereupon such as the said Captain Mom shall find to be fitting. So after the aforesaid proposal was taken into consideration and weighed, it was deemed not unreasonable and therefore deemed good to consent thereto, but upon favorable approval of their High Excellencies. Samarang in war council dated aforesaid, signed A. Roos, N. Steinmets, G. Mom.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast under Date 21st August 1741. Tagal, To the under-merchant Laurens Guothe, Resident there: Title. With the return of the ship Gasperdam we have received your letter of the 4th of this month, accompanied by some monthly papers, upon which there is nothing to answer, this is principally directed to make known that their High Excellencies have been pleased to relieve the governor Abraham Roos to Batavia and his Excellency to be replaced by the Mountain Captain Nathanael Steinmetsz in the capacity of provisional governor. Item, the first undersigned to be appointed as commissioner on behalf of the Dutch chartered Company over Java's northeast coast, likewise the second undersigned to the second in the aforementioned commission, which shall serve you in forming the papers and elsewhere, while you are further ordered to form a name roll of all native soldiers sent to you from Banjarmasin over Cheribon and the common land route as has already been done hereward, and to send the same directly to their High Excellencies in order that they may be entered in the soldier pay books, since their High Excellencies have informed us that you were ordered to send 300 heads of the native militia at cost hereward, and sometimes such could not happen as quickly as necessity requires due to lack of ships or smaller vessels. From Java's East Coast under Date 21st October 1741. Therefore we are sending the ship Meinberg to you for this purpose, hoping that you will not delay in expediting the aforementioned number of people; meanwhile this is accompanied by a letter from their High Excellencies directed to you, with which, with kind regards, I remain your good friends, was signed H. Verijsel, J. H. Theling, N. Steinmetz, G. Mom, H. Korenaer, C. Sibens, P. De Vos, J. Tonneman Junior, and R. De Clerq. In margin.

text_translated_detailed: Partonagara. Item: the Radeen Wasseengsario Diepanagara and Sodjaja, the Radeen Tommongong Soeradiningaat, have driven the enemy away, leaving forty dead Chinese and three Javanese. The aforementioned Radeen Tommongong is now encamped at Tuban, having received fourteen dead in the aforementioned action. Furthermore, I request to know how matters stand with Sumanap and Pamacossan. All that I have to say is contained in this letter. [Translated by me: was signed] J.s Lesueur per translator [below] agrees [signed] J: Dieler, E: gesw: Clerq. Translation of Javanese missive sent to the merchant and chief at Surabaya, Vincent van Wingerden, by the Radeen Tommongon Soeradiningaat of Sidaijoe there, brought on the 4th and received at Samarang on the 16th August 1741. After the customary preamble: I request that Your Excellency be pleased to provide me with cannons with their powder and shot, since the enemy is strong and well supplied with such ammunition. The enemy Chinese are estimated at three hundred men. The reason why I have not yet attacked them, from Java's south coast under date 21st August 1741, is that I am waiting for my people whom I have sent to Tuban to strike down all the enemy there, since I believe that it will not be as difficult there as here, because here there are many rivers to cross. All that I have to say for this time is contained in this letter. [Translated by me: signed] G: Dieler, E: gestr: clerq. To the Radeen Tommongong Tjacra Nagara, chief regent over the Company's lands Sumanap and Pama Cassan, together with his guardian Radeen Aijoe Soera Diningaat and her husband Aria Soeradiningrat. Customary preamble. Furthermore, the Pangerang Adipati Tjacraningaat has had three inhabitants of the village of Padusian, located in the district of Pama Cassaij, sent to me for some reasons, which are kept here in detention from Java's east coast under date 21st of September 1741, and after examination it has appeared that eleven days ago they were ordered by the cabajang of the village of Pogagang named Joeda Laxana to transport with a prau escort to Pasuruan the Javanese mantri Sudra Crati, subject to the Radeen Tommongong Sostra Winata, together with two men and two women of that nation besides a Pama Cassanerse woman from the village of Hoender married to one of the last-mentioned Javanese, and moreover they declare that at that time it was well known in Pama Cassan that the said regent was hostile toward the Company, and furthermore that strong easterly winds came to prevail until near the island of Sampang, where stepping ashore they were seized by Madurese, and subsequently brought back here. For this reason it appears to be of the utmost necessity to order Your Excellency to send the said Joeda Haxana without the slightest delay in security back here so that he can likewise be heard according to the requirements of justice, since it appears as if the same person, as a disloyal subject, maintains secret understanding with the enemy, which must be prevented and countered with all rigor in good time, meanwhile Your Excellency is ordered to first satisfy the delivery of cattle and coconut oil held by them for necessary food for this garrison, with proper payment; furthermore

text_translated_clean: regarding the cowardice of the Radeen Sourpanagara and Demang Mancoenagara, Your Excellency is pleased to order me to punish them because at the time when their peoples were still complete, they fled in a shameful manner before their enemies, which shall be made known to them in due time. Furthermore, Your Excellency recommends to me in person, as soon as possible, to come to Your Excellency with such a quantity of armed men as the aforementioned shall be in a state to offer resistance to the enemy, by which deeds I, according to your writings, shall win the favor of the Company in such a way that I shall obtain the name of my deceased father, which I hope to fulfill within a short time with God's help. From Java, East Coast, under Date 21st August 1741. I hope that the same shall have a good outcome; on the 19th of this month I think I shall undertake the journey to the Coast, therefore I request that Your Excellency be pleased to have the Madurese Pangerang requested that he allow my people to pass unhindered through his land, for I shall send half of my subjects overland. I request once more most urgently that my brother of that goodness be pleased, and provide me with a ship's cargo or as much more of that grain, preferably rice, as shall be possible. My brother shall thereby gain great favor with His High Excellency, greatly esteemed, and thereby make the trust in him all the greater. My brother can certainly, if he wishes, well agree to this fair request, since I am well informed that from Sidaijoe and Grissel a great quantity of paddy has been transported to Madura. Furthermore, be it known that it has pleased my brother to help free burghers in his residence with rice, which would give no good impression with His High Excellency, greatly esteemed, if I make this known, from which I hope my brother shall be pleased to relieve me through a speedy fulfillment, so that our intimate friendship may become all the greater and stronger. The bearer of this is the soldier Jan Balier. All that I have to say for this time is contained in this letter, which was sent to the Company's Comptoir Surabaya on the 10th August 1741. text_translated_detailed: The rice of the field is such that to begin anything against this fortress, time must reveal it, as well as what they are doing below this river, since one hears them daily knocking and chopping there, where we cannot easily pass through because of the marshes and thickets that are there, and we do not know how strongly they are holding themselves there. Furthermore, may it please Your Honour to know that just outside this fortress an 8-pound cannon was buried from Java's East Coast under Date 21st August 1741, which the first undersigned had dug up, had tested, and has been found good by the constable and his mate here, as appears from the report given thereof. I therefore request that Your Honour's permission be granted to have a gun carriage made for this, and then to place the same where it will be best, as well as for the writing off of some cans of arrack that have been distributed to the garrison through the much work that they have had to do daily on the coops. Title: We have received your letter and from it have seen with regret the distressed condition of the coast, which we hope will change shortly, especially since the natives of Sumanap and Pamacassan, as well as those of Surabaya, will be taken care of, to whose leaders further orders have been given in this regard. In the meantime, it is to be sustained that, since the enemies are somewhat far away, a quantity of rice will be able to be seized. Thus we order you to apply all diligence to gather that grain, while we have seen fit to authorize you to write off the amount of the aforementioned and paid transport costs overland to the coast, item of coops for the garrison for extra work delivered. Also, you will be provided with a gun carriage for an eight-pounder cannon that is buried under the earth. Furthermore, this serves as an escort for Captain Maximilian Constans, who is going over Surabaya to that place in order, in accordance with the esteemed orders of His High Excellencies, to replace Captain and Commandant Renicus Siersma, and after he has made the transport and delivery of a memorandum concerning the office to his successor, he must return here. And it further serves as notice and due observance that His Excellency has been pleased to relieve the Governor Roos to Batavia and to elect the first undersigned as commissioner of this coast, the second undersigned as second of the commission, and the warehouse master Nathanael Steinmetz as provisional governor. With which, under friendly greetings, we remain. Undersigned: Your good friends. Signed: H. Verijzel, J.H. Theling, N. Steinmetz, G. Mom, H. Koornaar Const, Sibens P. De Vos, J. Tonneman Junior, and R. D. Klerk. In the margin: Samarang, the 19th August 1741. Undersigned: Agrees: J. Bieler, E. G. Clercq. Samarang. To the Honourable

For the reason that the emperor, as it is rumored, believed that the aforementioned deceased had engaged in certain matters to the detriment of the imperial authority and to the advantage of the Esteemed Company. — That after the murder of the aforementioned pangerangs, 20 days ago, the tommongongs Djaja Soederga, Mangoe Nagara, and Soera Dipoera appeared in the lodge, strengthened with approximately 100 men, in order, as is customary, to pay the usual visits to the commandant, which was on Thursday, or the emperor's day, at which occasion, under the pretext of thanking [him] for a cup of tea water, the aforementioned tommongong Soederga drew his kris and with fury struck the aforementioned Captain a blow in his left arm and hip, whereupon the aforementioned van Velse drew his sword and with it dealt such a blow to that tommongong's neck that he fell to the ground. That immediately from the lodge, the assembled and fleeing Javanese were shot at in front of the fortress with cannon, when the gates were closed and the garrisons from the kraton [palace] had moved to the lodge, subsequently for 24 days continuous shooting and bombs were thrown, through which heavy fire the mortars of the Van Java's East Coast under Date 21st August 1741 burst, during which time the Javanese, joined with 500 Chinese, fortified themselves so strongly in the constructed entrenchments around the lodge that no one could come out or in, especially since the walls were completely knocked down by the emperor's heavy cannon, for which reason the commandant of Weltevreden sent a trumpeter to the Susuhunang [the Javanese ruler] in order to ask why His Majesty's Company lodge was being so pressed, seeing that it had been placed there at his grandfather's request and principally to assist him in all threatened calamities; whereupon the emperor had the commandant informed through the trumpeter that he knew of no contracts with the Honorable Company, but if they wished to obtain pardon they would have to surrender as prisoners of war, which the Captain was unwilling to agree to, and the garrisons absolutely did not wish to remain there any longer, so then General van Velse sent the trumpeter once more with the aforementioned scribe Nieuwenhuijsen to the emperor with a letter and without weapons, going to see if it was possible to bring about a mediation, in which the prince likewise in no way wished to agree, and had them return with the aforementioned message with the recommendation that they should henceforth place themselves under his obedience with the surrender of all their weapons, which that day the Captain and the further officers consulted about and decided to defend the lodge to the last man, from which

text_translated_detailed: Lord Hugo Verijsel, Commissioner over Java's Northeast Coast, by the Javanese Sodjaja, subordinate of the Pangerang Soppo Sono murdered at Kartasura. The relator says that upon the arrival of the Pangerang Toppo Sono at Kartasura, he was taken into service by that prince, and that at a certain time his master was requested by the regent to come to watch a bedaja performance, and having appeared there, the relator, after some time, saw that the aforementioned prince was seized and murdered, having been an eyewitness to this with his accompanying retinue, they sought to rescue their master from such violence, but this was not permitted by that pangerang with the expression "What do you wish to do! Let it happen and what God pleases"; when his relator's master was thus brought into the kraton and murdered there. That the relator subsequently placed himself under the subordinates of Radeen Aria Wiera Mangala, who, having learned of his brother's apprehension, fled to Samarang, and having arrived at Pattirongan was attacked by the Chinese and overcome and by them brought to Torbaja and murdered there; That the relator, after his master's death, was brought by the Chinese to Kartasura, where, being released again, he placed himself under the service of Radeen Natta Widjaja's subordinates, with whom he came here about a month ago. Furthermore, he declares that during the time of his journey he always kept company with a sergeant of the Buginese, Moehamat, since the same was also in the service of the aforementioned Radeen Natta Widjaja, whom he asked to seek a fortunate outcome, and thus over Caliberteng along the seashore with each other arrived here without further ado. Thus related at the head office, Samarang, 21st August, Year 1741. [Below] the

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast dated 8 August 1732, it was deemed proper to give notice first to Semarang, if possible, so that Your Excellency might come to its aid in time with the required assistance during the north wind. Furthermore, Your Excellency was recommended among other things regarding the territory and peaceful coexistence, so that the enemy thereby gains no advantage. Whereupon, commending Your Excellency, the Company's servants, and interests to God's gracious protection, we remain your good friend. [signed] Steinmetsz. [in margin] Japara, 13 August 1741. [Lower] Agreed, was signed J. d' Haas, Secretary Semarang. To the Honored and Esteemed Mister Abraham Roos, Chief Merchant and Commander on and along Java's Northeast Coast, together with the council. Title. My Last Respectful Letters from Java's East Coast dated 25 August 1741 from Your Honored Excellency have been of the 4th of this month by the ship Gaasperdam [Gasper Dam:]; since then I have had no occasion to be able to write to Your Honored Excellency, and yet now a prau from Cheribon [Cirebon:] has arrived here, so I have the honor to send herewith a copy of the missive of their High Excellencies as well as two of my humble letters to their High Excellencies dispatched, from which Your Honored Excellency will be able to see how matters stand here. The Javanese are not only increasing daily, but are also making bindings everywhere, which I cannot prevent because I can only muster no more than five hundred men, whereas they on the other hand are well fifteen thousand strong. And since I must see that daily large praus pass in sight of this lodge coming and going, which certainly bring people, provisions, or something else, I respectfully request the Point, Jalling the Peppertuin, the East Coast to be held and turned back. From Java's East Coast dated 26 August.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast, the 23rd of August 1711. Forty pieces of cannon from Rembang have been transported here by the Chinese, and concerning the further contents thereof, we refer you to our common letter of the 21st of this month sent to the Javanese Wira Tjoera, only noting that the same appears to confirm what was related. Before we conclude this matter, we take the liberty of reiterating our request contained in the common letter herewith sent regarding the Provisional Captain Commandant Gerrit Mom and the Lieutenants Jan Andries van Hohendorff, Jan Fredrik Vieravond, and H.K. Brulle. We can assure your High Excellency that the first is a valiant and capable man who has made himself so beloved not only among the Europeans but also among the native militia that we do not believe they would wish to stand under any other commander. And concerning the aforementioned Lieutenants, who according to common reports have given great signs of bravery. From Java's East Coast, the 25th of August 1741. Since we have no capable officers at hand to fill the Captain's positions, we must likewise beseech your High Excellency's great and powerful favor so that they may all be favored with their Acts of Improvement. Thereby we express our deep and obligated gratitude. Respectfully, your High Excellency's most obedient and humble servants. [Signed] M. Verijsel, J.H. Theling, N. Steinmets. text_original: Van Javas Oost Cust onder dato 25' 8ber 1741 Translaat Relaas Gedaan door de Iavaangse vrouwe Peradie Inwoonderesse van goemoelak De relatente segt dat den Riedeen de pattij Mitty Coesoema gecampeert zegt op Pate, — rongan Jtem nog derthien Tommagongs Romtom deese plaatse dog zegt den relahanten niet tekonnen zeggen hoe veel volk zij Lieden bij haar hebben maar dat 4000 Chineesen met 4 p s Carons die door haar van 'it Comptoir Rembangmaker waards sijn geevoerd bij haar sin dat derradeen depatti van Cartazoera heeft meede gebragt 50 p=s Carons mitsg 10. Europieese die bereeden zijn/ omdaan op te passen een door radja Nietie agt Euiro peesen die bewesten dellogie in een binting sijn geplaast: Dat de twee Tommagongs van Tagal na Derwaards sijn geretourneert uijt Meeder dat Sij hadden gehoort eenige 'sComps dienaaren van batavia overder land weg op marek waargoin na die plaats tekomen dat den wester strand gouverneur medera woorplaatse was vertrocken doordien hem was berigt dat aldaar meede Eenige Oost Cust onder dato 28 8ber 174. Van Iavas sComp dienaaren zouden aan Land geset werden dat den radeen depatti van gedagte was om den 15 van't zigt ot aanstaande Woensdag / te attacqueeren en soo indien hem dat mislukt als dan Dyntwinstigste zynde Woensdag daar aan volgende en daar na= den 25 zijnde Saturdags en bij aldien hij als dan zijn oogmerk niet keen berijken soo seutrij terug keeren na't kartaSoeras hoff: /onderstond/ aldus gedaan en gerlateerd den 11 van't Ligt Faban 1666 dan wel den 21 8ber 1740 /onderstond/ Getranslateert door mij /was getekend/ T: Leseur P„r Translateur / Lager accondeert / getekend/ & I:n : Bieler E G Clercq 6 Register van sodanige Papieren alser op heeden door den ondergeteekende op een gants nederige wijs Gesonden word aan tijn Edelheyt den hoog Edelen
text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast under date 25th of August 1741. Translation. Report given by the Javanese woman Peradie, inhabitant of Goemulak. The informant says that the leader of the party Mitty Coesoema is encamped, it is said, at Pate, Rongan. Item, furthermore thirteen Tommagongs [uncertain: local administrative officials] Romtom of this place, but the informant says he cannot say how many people they have with them, but that 4000 Chinese with 4 pieces of cannons, which were conveyed to them from the Rembang Company post, are with them, and that the leader of the party from Kartasura has also brought 50 pieces of cannons, together with 10 Europeans who are mounted, in order to keep watch, and one by Raja Nietie eight Europeans who are placed in a binting [uncertain: possibly a fortified structure] west of the lodge. That the two Tommagongs of Tagal have returned from there, from the report that they had heard that some of the Company's servants from Batavia were coming overland by way of the market to that place, and that the western coast governor, Medera's residence, had departed because he had been informed that there would also be some East Coast [text continues] under date 28th of August 174[1]. From Java's Company servants would be set ashore, and that the leader of the party was of the thought to attack on the 15th of the month or the coming Wednesday, and if that should fail for him, then the twenty-sixth, being Wednesday following thereafter, and thereafter the 25th, being Saturday, and if he should then not achieve his objective, he would return to the Kartasura court. /undersigned/ thus done and reported on the 11th of the month Faban 1666, or rather the 21st of August 1740 /undersigned/ Translated by me /was signed/ T: Leseur, Sworn Translator / Lower accorded / signed/ & I:n: Bieler E G Clercq. 6. Register of such papers as are hereby sent by the undersigned in a most humble manner to Your Excellency the High and Noble

Subordinate Court, Cuttack, the 29th of September 1740. From Java's East Coast, Batavia. To His Excellency the High and Esteemed Adriaan Valckenier, Governor-General, and the Esteemed Gentlemen Councillors of the Dutch Indies. Most High and Esteemed, Strict, Great and Venerable, Earnest, Steadfast, Wise, Provident, Most Generous, Widely Commanding Lord and Well-Esteemed Gentlemen.

The humble report to us in our most recent respectful letter to your High Excellency, Great and Venerable Councillors, of the 28th instant, we hereby cause to follow two copies of letters written by the Sumatran servants dated the 23rd and 24th before. The first was directed from the ship Beekvliet [Beech Fleet], by which the requested Captain of the Bugis, Posalamma, has arrived and then proceeded to Batavia, which vessel was loaded there with woodwork to the amount of ƒ1444:4:- [1444 guilders, 4 stuivers], as appears from the enclosed bill of lading and invoice. From Java's East Coast, the 29th of September 1747. Furthermore, that the enemy has strengthened their works up to the edge of the ravine of the mountain Laborren, and there displayed 3 pieces of cannons, with which our fortifications could not prevent the covered way, requesting to be supported with reinforcements. On which point the war council on the 26th deliberated and resolved that, since the Comptoir has much at stake in the Company's interests, the aforementioned servants should first be ordered, since their last letter was somewhat unclear, to provide a clearer and more detailed report on how matters then stand, and whether they, upon obtaining manpower, could prevent an open or defensive action against the rebelling rabble, so that a further resolution could be taken thereupon. Appearing in the enclosed Resolution, whereby it further appears that Commissioner Hugo Verijsel had proposed to the war council that the ships here present could not remain longer than until the end of the coming monsoon. From Java's East Coast, the 29th of September 1741, from Savees Port, will be able to remain.

text_original: Van Javas Oost Cust den 6 8ber 1714 Translaat Kelaas Gedaan door Babba Ledje Singadjaja en Brabba da poer van Samarang De Relateenten zeggen dat de Tommagong Wira Petra en Ariadjaja Lantika van Coedoes haar belast hebben om aan d E Comp berigt tedoen dat des wakste binting der vyanden is geleegen aan de baviaan op de weg na Patterongan leset door 506 Chineesen onder kepanjang haar hoofd Item tuijntjes benoorden de suerie Saaagten de Leeerplaats van voorm: reecenten waar nog meer na het noorden gelegert zynde twee mandere Regenten van damak padmara gara en Mathadepoera naer't Erff van Juffrouw Anthonij Legt gepasteert het eene hoofd der 700 Chineesen Singsing met 28 man Dat bescijden die plaatsen Leggen eenige Cartasorase regentien als radeen Malaijoe Koesoema Tommegang Atron birang Tommongong Mankoejoeda, Tommogong Van Java Pott Cust den 6 9ber 17100 t Natugoeda en Tommongong man koe Prodje daar benoorden Banga Calewoengoe Ingabey Awanga l van Candal het tweede hoofd de Chineese gen:t Laboekabee met 500 zyner meetie die sComp:s Logie hebben helpen inneemen agter de malijts Campong 6,06 Chineesen ondeer Laboek t'ampar: Dat Rad een de Pattijnatra CoeSoema geposteert legt op Patterongam Dat maas Brahim is aangesteld to't Regent van Passourouang dog als nu met 500 Chineesen gezonder na Sourabaija dit zouden altemaal Chineesen zyn die ter deser plaatse hebben gewoont /onstond aldus gedaan en de gerelateert ten hoofd Comptoir Camarang den 6 9ber 1741 /:onderstond/ getranslatieert door mij /was geteekend/ Lijsteerir p Translateur / Lager accorwas geteekend/ JBieler deert de Clercq Gt
text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast the 6th of August 1714 Translation Kelaas Done by Babba Ledje Singadjaja and Brabba da poer from Samarang The Relators say that the Tommagong Wira Petra and Ariadjaja Lantika from Coedoes have charged them to inform the Esteemed Company that the strongest fortification of the enemies is lying at the baviaan on the road to Patterongan occupied by 506 Chinese under kepanjang their head Item small gardens to the north of the suerie Saaagten the Learning place of the aforementioned relators where further to the north lying two manner Regents of damak padmara gara and Mathadepoera near the Estate of Mrs. Anthonij lies passed the one head of the 700 Chinese Singsing with 28 men That beside those places lying some Cartasorase regents as radeen Malaijoe Koesoema Tommegang Atron birang Tommongong Mankoejoeda, Tommogong From Java's East Coast the 6th of September 17100 t Natugoeda and Tommongong man koe Prodje there to the north Banga Calewoengoe Ingabey Awanga l from Candal the second head the Chinese called Laboekabee with 500 of his companions who helped the Company's Lodge take over behind the malijts Campong 6,06 Chinese under Laboek t'ampar: That Rad een de Pattijnatra CoeSoema posted lies on Patterongam That maas Brahim is appointed to the Regent of Passourouang but as now with 500 Chinese sent to Sourabaija these would all be Chinese who have lived at this place /understood/ thus done and related to the head Comptoir Camarang the 6th of September 1741 /:understood/ translated by me /was signed/ Lijsteerir p Translator / Below agrees /was signed/ JBieler deert de Clercq Gt

text_translated_detailed: India have been pleased to appoint Your Excellency as Commissioners and Governor over Java with a small number of ships and people who have arrived here to drive out the hostile Chinese and restore the river to the Gentlemen again, for which communication I express my thanks. From Java's East Coast under date 6 September 174[1]. Furthermore, we bring to Your Excellency's knowledge that you should have heard on the 14th through the Cartazoera's Commander all the Susuhanan's ministers distrusted, although many Chinese have been put to death by them and some brought in alive, and that distrust could not be avoided, although the prince could not perceive it sufficiently. Nevertheless, he allowed himself to appear outside the kraton [palace] at his usual time, after which the Emperor heard that the Commander had placed his confidence in the Pangerangs Toppa Sono and Wira Wangala. Item, the defection of the Madurese Pangerang Talcraningat, whereby he was greatly frightened, and from this it could be perceived that the Company's affairs were not lying well with the Susuhanan, which otherwise the matters have thus caused to become confused. From Java's East Coast under date 6 September 1741. Your Excellency has been pleased to request me, to which my person is too insignificant, to help seek Java's welfare together with the Company, for I am obliged to carry out the orders of my Sovereign, not only am I powerful to fulfill Your Excellency's request, but neither I nor the council of the party. The letter which you sent to me I did not dare to open, but showed it to the realm's administrator, who sent the same to Cartazoera. [Understood, translated by me, was signed, P. Lesueur, as Translator, Lower, agrees, was signed, In brief E.G. Clercq. To the Tommogou Wiera Sestra, First Regent of Damak, in the Aria Djaja Santia of Kudus. After customary preamble.

text_translated_detailed: From Java's East Coast, the 7th of September 1741. Translation of a Javanese letter sent to the Noble and Esteemed Gentlemen Hugo Verijsel and Johan Herman Theling, Commissioners on behalf of the chartered East India Company on and along Java's northeast coast, together with the Noble and Esteemed Gentleman N. text_translated_detailed: I would prefer to wait until my deed from the Susuhanan has been handed to me, when I am in a position to stand as surety for you gentlemen. Sakib Muhammad Usin has been appointed as head over 1000 priests. Consider again that you gentlemen have served the Company from Longstaff without receiving anything for it. It is true that as long as the Company's people show respect, but afterwards a dog is valued much more. What has Captain Sun done? From Java's East Coast, the 4th of September 1741. The Captain and Captain of the Malays have not served the Company without being rewarded for it. Look to yourselves in this regard and seek a way to be discharged from the Company. Join yourselves with the Susuhanan, who will reward you better. Do not be afraid—I shall bring you there. Why should you not be received in grace? The Muhammadans are the Christians of Cartasoera within the same circle and have obtained the Sultan's favor to lead that which the Susuhanan has with you. The lodge has not yet been taken. Yet you do not wish to leave the Company. According to Muhammad's providence, the time has now come that the Company shall be brought down, of which examples enough come forth. For what nations have been faithful to one another as the Chinese? The Company's rule has now, by God's will, come to an end with so many punishments. God has visited them all—signs that He has turned away from Java's East Coast, dated the 14th of September 1741. I shall expect an answer here first and shall come with some way for you gentlemen. To that end I shall remain with Salied Muhammad's Sintadje Muhammad mat Taram at Patterongan, and if you gentlemen have been troubled by anything from the Chinese, do not be afraid there, for they dare not do it, as they have no one to bring forward.

To His High Excellency the High Noble Lord Adriaan Valckenier, Governor General, and the Noble Lords, Councillors of the Dutch Indies. From Java's East Coast on 3 September 1741. High Noble, strict, greatly esteemed, earnest, faithful, wise, provident, most generous, widely commanding lord and well-esteemed lords. Just as we had the honor on the 9th of this month to report to your High Excellency the happy and unexpected victory of the Esteemed Company, we sent two express vessels for that purpose. So we can report again today that although this [victory], although it cost us more dead and wounded than in previous days, we nevertheless do not hesitate to solicit your High Excellency again with the taking of the pass, which was fortified by ours at three different places and finally was overrun. The first and last stronghold, where the Chinese had fortified themselves, was done in such a decisive manner that no one could believe it unless one saw it. From Java's East Coast on 13 September 1741, we would very gladly have held the provisions with satisfaction.

To His Excellency the Most Noble and Esteemed Lord Adriaan Valckenier, Governor General, and the Noble Lords, Councillors of the Dutch Indies.

Most Noble, Esteemed, Mighty, Honorable, Earnest, Valiant, Wise, Provident, Most Generous, Wide-governing Lord and Well-Esteemed Gentlemen,

When we took possession of Java's East Coast on the 13th of September 1741, of the sea villages Caligawaen and Torbay, we brought some Javanese people, both men and women, whom we first sent to the Regent Soeradimangala with the request that they be treated kindly, and we sought to learn of the condition of the enemy army. Upon this, he provided us with the following account, to the tenor of which we shall conduct ourselves briefly. The victories achieved by the Company on the 7th and 9th of this month will surely have become clear to Your Excellency from our general letters sent for that purpose. Likewise, Your Excellency will have learned beforehand of the conquest achieved today in our meeting with the Samarang Javanese and those of the Council Regent Natta Coesuma, contained in our submissive letter of the 13th. Truly, circumstances which cause us great embarrassment, since we do not yet find ourselves equipped with Your Excellency's Instructions, and consequently do not know how we ought to conduct ourselves in one matter or another. We humbly request that it may please Your Excellency to have the same sent to us at the first opportunity.
